summary: The paper constructs motives over Q attached to symmetric power moments of Kloosterman sums and proves that their L-functions continue meromorphically and satisfy the functional equations conjectured by Broadhurst and Roberts. Its central result, and the reason for its title, is a Hodge-theoretic one: the mixed Hodge structure H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) has all Hodge numbers equal to 0 or 1, which is exactly the regularity of the associated Galois representations, and that is what makes Patrikis and Taylor's potential-automorphy theorem applicable. The route is as follows. Over a finite field, Z_k(p;T) is the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on the compactly supported étale cohomology of Sym^k Kl₂, and M_k(p;T) the same on the middle cohomology, which is pure of weight k+1 by Weil II. Over a field of characteristic zero, the Kloosterman connection Kl_{n+1} = π_*E^f is the rank-(n+1) connection of the hypergeometric operator (z∂_z)^{n+1} - z, regular at 0 and of pure slope 1/(n+1) at infinity; a Thom–Sebastiani argument identifies the de Rham cohomology of its symmetric powers with isotypic parts of the twisted de Rham cohomology of a torus. Those cohomologies are a priori only exponential mixed Hodge structures in the sense of Kontsevich and Soibelman; after pulling back along the cover z = t^{n+1}, which turns the function into a product t·g, the appendix's criterion shows they are classical mixed Hodge structures and that the irregular Hodge filtration is the Hodge filtration. The middle one is then identified with a piece of the cohomology of the hypersurface 𝒦 ⊂ G_m^{kn} cut out by g^{⊞ k}, which makes it the Hodge realization of a Nori motive 𝑴_k; the Hodge numbers are computed for n = 1 by an explicit basis of the de Rham cohomology and the toric interpretation of the irregular Hodge filtration. Finally the ℓ-adic realizations are computed at the bad primes, the p-adic realization is compared with rigid cohomology, and potential automorphy gives the analytic continuation. What the atlas lacks: everything on the Hodge side. There is no D-module theory, no Fourier transform of D-modules, no mixed Hodge modules, no exponential mixed Hodge structures and no irregular Hodge filtration; and there is nothing on Kloosterman sheaves or connections, their symmetric powers or the motives of their moments. What the atlas plans and this paper uses: mixed Hodge structures with their weight filtration (the Tau Ceti Hodge-structures roadmap), nearby and vanishing cycles in the ℓ-adic and topological settings, the perverse intermediate extension and Poincaré duality, Weil II, rigid cohomology with its Frobenius, de Rham/semistable/crystalline p-adic representations, and weakly compatible systems with their Weil–Deligne representations. The completion reads §§2.2–5 and the appendix at proof level. It names the inputs those proofs use as further items: the explicit structure of Kl₂, the toric and non-degenerate compactifications, the log-pole description of the irregular Hodge filtration, the geometry of 𝒦 over Z and over F̄_p, the Picard–Lefschetz and discriminant computations at the bad primes, the local L-factors, conductors and ε-factors, and the p-adic comparison and Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula. Two further source routes are added: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.2 takes Illusie's non-ordinary quadratic singularity, and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 takes the filtration lemma 5.40. Tau Ceti's mixed Hodge structures make one more item a library item. Seven misprints are recorded; none affects a stated result.

items.name: Dirichlet characters, the Legendre and Kronecker symbols, and the Gamma function
items.statement: The Legendre symbol (p/3), Dirichlet characters, the Riemann zeta function and Euler's Gamma function, as they occur in the local factors and the gamma factor.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.1 and Corollary 5.30; arXiv v5 pp. 2–3 and p. 52
items.note: Mathlib has Dirichlet characters, the Legendre and Jacobi symbols, the Riemann zeta function and the Gamma function. Mathlib also has additive characters (AddChar, Mathlib/Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean:70) and Gauss sums (gaussSum, Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:72) but not Kloosterman sums. Tau Ceti has pure and mixed Hodge structures (item 2). Neither library has D-modules, perverse sheaves, Hodge modules, étale or rigid cohomology, nearby cycles or Galois representations of this kind (declaration index at the pins searched for DModule, Holonomic, Perverse, HodgeModule, EtaleCohomology, NearbyCycle, VanishingCycle, Kloosterman, Isocrystal, RigidCohomology, WeilDeligne, Motive).

items.name: Mixed Hodge structures with their weight and Hodge filtrations
items.statement: Pure and mixed Q-Hodge structures, the Hodge decomposition of the complexification, polarizations, the weight filtration, Tate twists Q(n), and the strictness of morphisms.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.3 and throughout; the target category of Theorem 3.2; arXiv v5 p. 6
items.note: Read at Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructure (TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Structure.lean:75), its Hodge decomposition HodgeStructureOn.decomposition (Decomposition.lean:176), Polarization (Polarization.lean:157), MixedHodgeStructure (Mixed/Basic.lean:72: rational increasing weight filtration, complex decreasing Hodge filtration, pure graded pieces), Deligne strictness Hom.range_inf_F_eq_map_F and Hom.range_inf_WQ_eq_map_WQ (Mixed/Strictness.lean:108, 129), the Tate structure tate (Tate/Basic.lean:90) and tateMixed (Mixed/Basic.lean:307), and Tate twists HodgeStructureOn.tateTwist (Tate/Twist.lean:57). These realise the L0 and L2 milestones of the Tau Ceti Hodge-structures roadmap that the checkpoint listed as planning this item. Tau Ceti's structures live on an integral module with rational and complex models; a Q-mixed Hodge structure, which is what this paper uses, is the case of a rational module. What the paper needs on top is Saito's theory of mixed Hodge modules and the exponential variant, which nothing plans.

items.name: Nearby and vanishing cycles with their monodromy
items.statement: The nearby-cycle and vanishing-cycle functors attached to a function, the monodromy operator and its logarithm N, and the monodromy weight filtration centred at a given integer.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §3 and the appendix, where ψ and φ are taken in the sense of mixed Hodge modules; arXiv v5 pp. 16–18 and 61–63
items.note: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 and LPV.6 plan nearby and vanishing cycles and their perverse form, and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.3 the étale version. The Hodge-module refinement, in which ψ and φ carry mixed Hodge structures, is part of the mixed-Hodge-module theory that nothing plans.

items.name: The perverse intermediate extension and middle cohomology
items.statement: For an open immersion j and a perverse sheaf or holonomic module F, the intermediate extension j_{!*}F as the image of j_! F → j_* F, and the middle cohomology of F on the open as the image of cohomology with compact support in ordinary cohomology.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.2 and Corollary 2.15, where the middle de Rham cohomology is identified with the cohomology of the intermediate extension on P¹; arXiv v5 p. 4 and p. 15
items.note: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5 plans the perverse category and the intermediate extension, EDC.2 Poincaré duality. The paper needs the same notions for holonomic D-modules and for mixed Hodge modules, which is part of the missing D-module theory.

items.name: Weil II: weights of étale cohomology and purity of the middle extension
items.statement: For a lisse sheaf pure of weight w on a variety over a finite field, the étale cohomology with compact support has weights ≤ w + i and the ordinary étale cohomology has weights ≥ w + i; consequently the middle-extension cohomology is pure.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.2, where the purity of weight k+1 of the middle étale cohomology of Sym^k Kl₂ is deduced; arXiv v5 pp. 4–5 and 24
items.note: DeligneWeightsAndPurity plans Weil I and the Weil II results it needs; WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.5–34.6 plan Weil II and its purity applications. The paper uses the statement as a black box.

items.name: Rigid cohomology with and without compact support, and its Frobenius structure
items.statement: For a variety over a finite field with an overconvergent F-isocrystal as coefficients, rigid cohomology and rigid cohomology with compact support, with their Frobenius endomorphism, finiteness and Poincaré duality.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §3.2.2, arXiv v5 pp. 25–26, and §5.1.5, pp. 49–51, where H¹_rig,mid(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl₂) is the object compared with the p-adic realization
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3–RD.5 plan overconvergent isocrystals, rigid cohomology with compact support, finiteness and duality; RD.6 the trace formula and p-adic weights; RD.7 the crystalline comparison. The Kloosterman F-isocrystal itself is a separate missing item.

items.name: de Rham, semistable and crystalline p-adic representations
items.statement: Fontaine's period rings B_dR, B_st and B_crys, the associated functors, and the notions of de Rham, semistable and crystalline p-adic Galois representation with their Hodge–Tate weights.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 5.23, where V_{k,p} is shown to be de Rham and semistable or crystalline; arXiv v5 p. 49
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory plans the period rings and the comparison theorems; R06.5 owns the geometric comparison theorems. The paper uses them for the representation attached to its motive.

items.name: Weakly compatible systems and their Weil–Deligne representations
items.statement: A weakly compatible system of ℓ-adic Galois representations of Gal(Q-bar/Q) with a finite ramification set, the Weil–Deligne representation WD_p attached to each member at a prime p, purity of a Weil–Deligne representation, regularity, and odd essential self-duality.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.2, arXiv v5 p. 56, in the hypotheses of Theorem 5.38
items.note: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 is titled compatible systems and reusable transport and plans exactly this interface. The Patrikis–Taylor theorem that consumes it is a separate missing item.

items.name: Holonomic D-modules on a curve and their six operations
items.statement: The ring of algebraic differential operators on a smooth affine variety, holonomic and regular holonomic modules over it, the derived pushforward and pullback for the immersions j_0: G_m → A¹ and j_∞, the functors j_! , j_* and the intermediate extension j_{!*}, duality, and the slope decomposition of a meromorphic connection at an irregular singular point. For a connection E on G_m with a regular singularity at 0, dim H¹_dR(G_m, E) − dim H⁰_dR(G_m, E) = irr_∞(E), the irregularity number at infinity (the Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula for connections, Katz 1990, Th. 2.9.9), and the kernel of j_†E → j_{†+}E has punctual support (Katz 1990, Prop. 2.9.8).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Appendix A.1, the section «Notation and results from the theory of D-modules»; arXiv v5 pp. 59–61
items.note: The paper's appendix fixes the conventions and quotes the results it uses; nothing in the atlas plans D-modules at all. The slope theory at an irregular singularity is used in Proposition 2.4 (2) and Proposition 4.6 (3). The index formula gives (4.11), dim H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) = ⌊(k+1)/2⌋, and the punctual-support statement is what makes the middle cohomology equal to the cohomology of the intermediate extension (Corollary 2.15).

items.name: The Fourier transform of a D-module on the affine line and its localized form
items.statement: The Fourier transformation FT on holonomic D-modules on A¹, exchanging t and ∂_t with τ and -∂_τ, and the localized Fourier transform ℱ = j_0^* FT j_{0*} on G_m, which preserves holonomicity and sends a regular holonomic module to a module smooth on G_m with a regular singularity at 0 and slopes in {0,1} at infinity. Fourier transformation commutes with duality up to the involution t ↦ -t.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §2.1, and Appendix A.1; arXiv v5 pp. 10–11 and 60–61
items.note: This is the engine of the recursive description of the Kloosterman connections and of the whole Hodge-theoretic argument, which reads Sym^k Kl-tilde as the restriction of a Fourier transform of a mixed Hodge module.

items.name: Mixed Hodge modules on a curve, their weights and the functor Π
items.statement: Saito's abelian category MHM(X) of (graded-polarizable, algebraic) mixed Hodge modules on a smooth complex variety X, with objects M^H = (M, F_•M, 𝓕_Q, α) consisting of a regular holonomic left D_X-module, a good filtration, a Q-perverse sheaf and an isomorphism ᵖDR M ≅ 𝓕_C, and the conventions used in the paper: pure polarizable Hodge modules of weight w (via the side-changing functor, Saito 1988, 5.1.6 and 5.2.10), with a smooth pure module of weight w being a polarizable variation of weight w − dim X; the weight filtration; the six operations on D^b(MHM(X)) (f_*, f_!, f^*, f^!, duality 𝐃 with 𝐃 ᵖQ_U^H ≅ ᵖQ_U^H(−d), ⊠), with f_! decreasing and f_* increasing weights (Saito 1990, (4.5.2)); the localization triangles i_*i^!M → M → M[*D] and M[!D] → M → i_*i^*M (Saito 1990, (4.4.1)); the nearby and vanishing cycle functors ψ_f = ψ_{f,1} ⊕ ψ_{f,≠1} and φ_{f,1} with can, var and N = var∘can, whose weight filtration on ψ_{f,1} is the relative monodromy filtration; on a curve, the compatibility of the Hodge filtration with the Kashiwara–Malgrange filtration, rk gr^p_F M = dim gr^p_F ψ_f M (Saito 1988, 3.2.1), and W_ℓ ψ_f M = ψ_f W_{ℓ+1} M at a non-singular point; the semisimplicity of polarizable pure Hodge modules, a pure object decomposing by strict support (used in Lemma 2.24 and Example A.2); and the lift of additive *-convolution N₁ ⋆ N₂ = s_*(N₁ ⊠ N₂) and of the projector Π to MHM(A¹).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Appendix A.2, the section «Notation and results from the theory of mixed Hodge modules»; arXiv v5 pp. 61–63
items.note: The appendix only fixes notation and quotes Saito; no step of the paper reproves any part of the theory. The proofs of §§2.3, 3.1, 4.3 and the appendix use exactly the facts listed, in dimension kn + 1 for the pushforwards f_* and f_! to A¹ and on curves for the nearby-cycle statements. Nothing in the atlas plans mixed Hodge modules, so the new roadmap must build them (see the route's brief).

items.name: Local structure of a mixed Hodge module at a point (Example A.2)
items.statement: For U = A¹ and f the identity, a pure Hodge module M^H decomposes as M₁^H ⊕ M₂^H with M₁ having no section supported at 0 and M₂ supported at 0; then H⁰ i_* i^! M₁^H = 0, H¹ i_* i^! M₂^H = 0, H⁰ i_* i^! M₂^H ≅ i_* i^! M₂^H, and H¹ i_* i^! M₁^H is isomorphic to the cokernel of the variation map on vanishing cycles.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Example A.2; arXiv v5 p. 62
items.note: The local computation that feeds the weight statements of Corollary A.31; the filtration conventions for left modules are fixed here.

items.name: Localization sequences for the constant Hodge module along a divisor (Example A.3)
items.statement: For a reduced divisor D ⊂ U with structure morphism a_D, writing Q_D^H for the shifted constant Hodge module, there are an isomorphism i^* Q_U^H ≅ Q_D^H and an exact sequence 0 → i_* Q_D^H → Q_U^H[!D] → Q_U^H → 0; if D is smooth there is in addition i^! Q_U^H[1] ≅ Q_D^H(-1) and the dual exact sequence 0 → Q_U^H → Q_U^H[*D] → i_* Q_D^H(-1) → 0.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Example A.3; arXiv v5 p. 63
items.note: These two sequences are what produce the localization long exact sequences of Example A.20, and hence the description of the middle Hodge structure by the hypersurface 𝒦.

items.name: Exponential mixed Hodge structures
items.statement: The category EMHS of Kontsevich and Soibelman: the full subcategory of MHM(A¹_θ) of objects whose underlying perverse sheaf has vanishing global cohomology, equivalently those N^H with N^H ≅ Π_θ(N^H), where Π_θ(N^H) = N^H ⋆ j_!O^H_{G_m} is an exact projector onto EMHS, left adjoint to the inclusion, with a natural morphism N^H → Π_θ(N^H) whose kernel and cokernel are constant (the kernel's D-module being the maximal constant submodule of N); its tensor structure induced by ⋆, with Π(N₁^H) ⋆ Π(N₂^H) = Π(N₁^H ⋆ N₂^H); its weight filtration W^EMHS_n Π(N^H) = Π(W_n N^H), strictly compatible with the tensor product (Kontsevich–Soibelman, Prop. 4.3); and the de Rham fibre functor Π(N^H) ↦ H¹_dR(A¹_θ, N ⊗ E^θ), which is exact, detects zero objects, and carries the weight filtration defined as the image of H¹_dR(A¹_θ, W_•N ⊗ E^θ).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Appendix A.3, with Remark A.6 for the weight filtration; arXiv v5 pp. 63–64
items.note: The checkpoint described EMHS as the objects with no subobject or quotient supported at a point; that is not the definition and is false (j_!Q_{G_m}[1] lies in EMHS and contains i_{0*}Q). The definition above is the paper's.

items.name: The weight filtration of an exponential mixed Hodge structure (Remark A.6)
items.statement: There is a functorial morphism W_n N^H → W_n^EMHS N^H when N^H = Π(N^H); if N^H is mixed of weights ≤ n, respectively ≥ n, in MHM(A¹), then Π(N^H) is mixed of weights ≤ n, respectively ≥ n, in EMHS; in particular Π of a pure Hodge module of weight n is a pure object of EMHS of weight n, even though it is only mixed of weights ≥ n in MHM(A¹).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Remark A.6; arXiv v5 p. 64
items.note: The mismatch between the two weight filtrations is exactly what the whole appendix is for, and what makes Theorem 3.2 a real theorem rather than a formality.

items.name: The irregular Hodge filtration
items.statement: For a mixed Hodge module N^H on A¹_t, the filtration irrF^• on H¹_dR(A¹_t, N ⊗ E^t) defined as the image of H¹_dR(P¹, irrF^• j_{∞*}(N ⊗ E^t)), following Deligne's idea as developed by Sabbah and by Esnault, Sabbah and Yu.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Appendix A.3, with Proposition A.10, arXiv v5 pp. 64–65
items.note: The irregular Hodge filtration is the invariant that makes sense for an exponential mixed Hodge structure even when it is not a classical one; for those that are classical it agrees with the Hodge filtration, by Proposition A.13.

items.name: The bifiltered de Rham fibre factors through Π and is strict (Proposition A.10)
items.statement: The natural morphism H¹_dR(P¹, irrF^• j_{∞*}(N ⊗ E^t)) → H¹_dR(A¹_t, N ⊗ E^t) is injective; defining irrF^• on the target as its image, the functor N^H ↦ (H¹_dR(A¹_t, N ⊗ E^t), irrF^•, W_•) from MHM(A¹_t) to bifiltered vector spaces factors through Π, and every morphism of MHM(A¹_t), or of EMHS, induces a strictly bifiltered morphism.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition A.10; arXiv v5 p. 65
items.note: Strictness is what lets the Hodge numbers be read off the graded pieces, and factoring through Π is what makes the de Rham fibre an invariant of the exponential mixed Hodge structure.

items.name: Mixed Hodge structures form a full tensor subcategory of EMHS (Lemma A.12)
items.statement: The functor Π ∘ i_{0!} from mixed Hodge structures to EMHS is compatible with tensor products and makes MHS a full tensor subcategory of EMHS; moreover W_• Π_θ(i_{0!}V^H) = Π_θ(i_{0!}W_• V^H), so the two weight filtrations agree on classical objects.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Lemma A.12; arXiv v5 p. 65
items.note: Fullness is what makes the natural maps between the three cohomologies of a pair (U,f) morphisms of mixed Hodge structures once they are known to be classical.

items.name: When an exponential mixed Hodge structure is classical, the two filtrations agree (Proposition A.13)
items.statement: If N^H in MHM(A¹_t) has Π(N^H) in MHS, then the bifiltered vector space (H¹_dR(A¹_t, N ⊗ E^t), irrF^•, W_•) is naturally isomorphic to the one attached to the mixed Hodge structure φ_{t,1}N^H.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition A.13; arXiv v5 p. 65
items.note: This is the bridge the paper needs: it can compute the irregular Hodge filtration geometrically, and then read the answer as the ordinary Hodge filtration.

items.name: The exponential mixed Hodge structures of a pair (U,f)
items.statement: For a smooth quasi-projective U with a regular function f and an integer r, the objects H^r(U,f) = Π_t((Q_U^H)^r_*), H^r_c(U,f) = Π_t((Q_U^H)^r_!) and H^r_mid(U,f) = Π_t((Q_U^H)^r_mid) of EMHS, with de Rham fibres the twisted de Rham cohomologies H^r_dR(U, E^f), H^r_{dR,c}(U, E^f) and H^r_{dR,mid}(U, E^f), each bifiltered by irrF^• and W_•.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Definition A.18, after Kontsevich–Soibelman §5; Example A.15 for f = 0; arXiv v5 p. 66
items.note: These are the objects the whole paper computes with. For f = 0 they are the usual mixed Hodge structures on the cohomology of U.

items.name: Weights of the cohomology of a pair (U,f) (Proposition A.19)
items.statement: For U of dimension d, H^d_c(U,f) is mixed of weights ≤ d, H^d(U,f) is mixed of weights ≥ d, and H^d_mid(U,f) is pure of weight d; moreover the map gr^W_d H^d_c(U,f) → gr^W_d H^d(U,f) is an isomorphism if and only if H^d_mid(U,f) = W_d H^d(U,f).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition A.19; arXiv v5 p. 66
items.note: The equivalence in the second half is the criterion used to prove the purity statement of Theorem 3.2, and it is what reduces that theorem to a dimension count.

items.name: Localization long exact sequences for a pair (U,f) (Example A.20)
items.statement: For a divisor D on which f vanishes there is a long exact sequence ··· → H^{r-1}_c(D) → H^r_c(U\D, f) → H^r_c(U,f) → H^r_c(D) → ···, and, if D is smooth, a dual one ··· → H^{r-2}(D)(-1) → H^r(U,f) → H^r(U\D,f) → H^{r-1}(D)(-1) → ···.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Example A.20; arXiv v5 p. 67
items.note: These are the sequences that identify the cohomology of a pair with the cohomology of the zero locus of f, and hence give the motive of Theorem 3.8 its geometric description.

items.name: The basic computation H^k(G_m^k, x₁+···+x_k) (Example A.22)
items.statement: For each k ≥ 1 there are isomorphisms H^k(G_m^k, x₁+···+x_k) ≅ Q(-k) and H^k_c(G_m^k, x₁+···+x_k) ≅ Q(0), obtained from the vanishing of H^r(A¹_x, x) and H^r_c(A¹_x, x) and the localization sequences.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Example A.22; arXiv v5 pp. 67–68
items.note: The seed of every weight computation in the paper, and the source of the Tate summand Q(-k-1) that appears in the top weight of H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂).

items.name: Exponential mixed Hodge structures of the form (A¹ × V, tg) are classical (Theorem A.24)
items.statement: If U = A¹_t × V with V smooth quasi-projective and f = tg for a regular function g on V, and M_V^H is a mixed Hodge module on V, then for N_U^H = Q^H_{A¹} ⊠ M_V^H the exponential mixed Hodge structures H^r(U, N^H, f) and H^r_c(U, N^H, f) belong to MHS for every r, and their bifiltered de Rham fibres underlie the corresponding mixed Hodge structures; the same holds for the localized and dual-localized variants.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem A.24, compare Yu, Theorem 3.3 and Fresán–Jossen, Lemma 6.5.3; arXiv v5 pp. 68–70
items.note: This is the criterion that makes Theorem 3.2 possible: after the double cover the function becomes t·g, and the theorem applies verbatim.

items.name: The cohomology of (A¹ × V, tg) is the cohomology of the zero locus (Example A.27)
items.statement: Applying Theorem A.24 to the constant Hodge module with 𝒦 = g^{-1}(0), the mixed Hodge structure H^r_c(A¹_t × V, tg) is isomorphic to H^r_c(A¹_t × 𝒦), and by the Künneth formula to H^{r-2}_c(𝒦)(-1).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Example A.27; arXiv v5 pp. 70–71
items.note: The step that turns a twisted de Rham cohomology into the cohomology of an honest algebraic variety, and hence gives the motive 𝑴_k.

items.name: Fourier transform of a mixed Hodge module and the cohomology of a pair (Lemma A.28, Notation A.29)
items.statement: The de Rham fibres of H^{j+1}(A¹_t × A¹_τ, N^H, tτ) and of its compactly supported analogue are H^j_dR(A¹_t, FT M) for j = 0,1 and H^j_{dR,c}(A¹_t, FT M) for j = 1,2, and zero otherwise; one writes H^j(A¹_t, FT M^H) and H^j_c(A¹_t, FT M^H) for the corresponding mixed Hodge structures, with their bifiltered de Rham fibres.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Lemma A.28 and Notation A.29; arXiv v5 p. 71
items.note: This is what gives the Fourier transform of a mixed Hodge module a Hodge-theoretic meaning, which is how §3 transports the weight information from M-tilde to the cohomology of Sym^k Kl-tilde.

items.name: The Fourier transform and the stalk at the origin (Theorem A.30)
items.statement: For every mixed Hodge module M^H on the affine line, the mixed Hodge structures H^j(A¹_t, FT M^H) and H^j(i_0^! M^H) are isomorphic, where i_0 is the inclusion of the origin.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem A.30; arXiv v5 pp. 71–72
items.note: The general form of the comparison; the next corollary is the case actually used.

items.name: Weights of the Fourier transform of a pure Hodge module (Corollary A.31)
items.statement: Let M^H be a pure object of MHM(A¹_τ) of weight w whose underlying D-module M has no non-zero section supported at the origin (so M is an intermediate extension at 0). Then H^{j+1}_dR(A¹_t, FT_τM) = 0 for j ≠ 0, and (1) H¹(A¹_t, FT_τM^H) is isomorphic to the mixed Hodge structure coker[N: ψ_{τ,1}M^H → ψ_{τ,1}M^H(−1)]; (2) if 0 is not a singular point of M, H¹(A¹_t, FT_τM^H) is pure of weight w+1 and dim gr^p_{irrF}H¹_dR(A¹_t, FT_τM) = rk gr^{p−1}_F M; and (3) if moreover M has no non-zero constant submodule, there is an exact sequence 0 → M^H → Π_τ(M^H) → M'^H → 0 in MHM(A¹) with M'^H constant of weights ≥ w+1 and dim gr^p_{irrF}gr^W_ℓ H¹_dR(A¹_t, FT_τM') = rk gr^{p−1}_F gr^W_{ℓ−1}M' for all ℓ, p.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary A.31; arXiv v5 pp. 72–73
items.note: The computational heart of the appendix: it converts weights of the Fourier transform into the monodromy filtration on nearby cycles, which is what §3 computes for M-tilde.

items.name: Kloosterman sums, their symmetric powers and moments
items.statement: For a prime p, a non-trivial additive character ψ of F_p and a ∈ F_q^×, the Kloosterman sum Kl₂(a;q) = Σ_{x ∈ F_q^×} ψ(tr(x + a/x)); by Weil, Kl₂(a;q) = -(α_a + β_a) with α_aβ_a = q and |α_a| = |β_a| = √q. The k-th symmetric power is Kl₂^{Sym^k}(a;q) = Σ_{i=0}^k α_a^i β_a^{k-i}, the moment is m₂^k(q) = Σ_{a ∈ F_q^×} Kl₂^{Sym^k}(a;q), and Z_k(p;T) = exp(Σ_n m₂^k(p^n)T^n/n) is a polynomial with integer coefficients.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.1; arXiv v5 pp. 2–3
items.note: The moments are rational integers independent of ψ, although the individual symmetric powers are not. The convention makes Kl₂^{Sym¹} the negative of Kl₂. Mathlib has additive characters and Gauss sums but no Kloosterman sums; Weil's bound is item 66.

items.name: The L-function of symmetric power moments and its completion
items.statement: M_k(p;T) is the polynomial obtained from Z_k(p;T) by removing its trivial factors, all of whose roots have absolute value p^{-(k+1)/2}. For odd k = 2m+1 and S the set of odd primes ≤ k, L_k(s) = ∏_{p ∉ S} M_k(p;p^{-s})^{-1}, convergent for Re(s) > (k+3)/2, and Λ_k(s) = (cond_k/π^m)^{s/2} ∏_{j=1}^m Γ((s-j)/2) ∏_p L_k(p;s) with cond_k the product of the square-free parts of 1,3,5,…,k. For even k, S is the set of primes ≤ k/2, cond'_k is the product of the odd radicals of 2,4,…,k, and Λ'_k(s) is the analogous completion away from 2.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.1; arXiv v5 pp. 2–4
items.note: The bad local factors at p ∈ S are given explicitly in §5; at p = 2 for even k they are left as an unknown reciprocal polynomial L_k(2;T) with an exponent r_k.

items.name: Meromorphic continuation and functional equation, odd case (Theorem 1.2)
items.statement: For odd k, L_k(s) admits a meromorphic continuation to C and Λ_k(s) = Λ_k(k+2-s).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 1.2; arXiv v5 p. 3
items.note: The first main theorem, and the odd half of the Broadhurst–Roberts conjecture; previously known only for k ≤ 8.

items.name: Meromorphic continuation and functional equation, even case (Theorem 1.3)
items.statement: For even k, L_k(s) extends meromorphically to C, and there are a sign ε_k ∈ {±1}, an integer r_k ≥ 0 and a reciprocal of a polynomial with rational coefficients L_k(2;T) such that Λ_k(s) = 2^{r_k s/2}L_k(2;2^{-s})Λ'_k(s) satisfies Λ_k(s) = ε_k Λ_k(k+2-s).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 1.3; arXiv v5 p. 4
items.note: The even half. The local invariants at p = 2 are not made explicit; Broadhurst and Roberts conjecture r_k = ⌊k/6⌋ and ε_k = (-1)^{t_k} for an explicit t_k, and §5 explains how the terms of t_k other than ⌊k/8⌋ match the computations at odd primes of S and at infinity.

items.name: The Kloosterman sheaf and the cohomological interpretation of the moments
items.statement: For ℓ ≠ p, the Artin–Schreier sheaf AS_ψ on A¹_{F_p} and the Kloosterman sheaf Kl₂ = Rπ_! f^* AS_ψ[1] on G_m, where π and f = x + z/x are the two maps out of G_m². It is lisse of rank two, tame at 0, wild at infinity, pure of weight one, and the forget-supports map is an isomorphism. Then Z_k(p;T) = det(1 - F_p T | H¹_{ét,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂)) and M_k(p;T) is the same determinant on the middle cohomology, which by Weil II is pure of weight k+1. More generally (§3.2.1), for n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≠ p, Kl_{n+1} = Rπ_*AS_{ψ(f)}[n] on G_{m,F_p}, with f(z, x) = x₁ + ⋯ + x_n + z/(x₁⋯x_n), is a lisse sheaf of rank n+1 in degree 0, pure of weight n, whose geometric Frobenius at z ∈ G_m(F_q) has trace (−1)^n Kl_{n+1}(z;q) (Deligne, SGA 4½, Th. 7.4 and 7.8), and Kl-tilde_{n+1} = [n+1]^*Kl_{n+1} ≅ Rπ-tilde_*AS_{ψ(f-tilde)}[n]. Over F̄_p the exact sequence relating H¹_c and H¹ of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} to inertia invariants and coinvariants at 0 and ∞, with Weil II (Lemma 1.8.1), gives gr^W_{kn+1}H¹_{ét,c} ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}H¹_ét, whose image is the middle cohomology (also Yun, Lemma 2.5.4); cohomology is concentrated in degree one for p odd, or p = 2 and n odd.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.2, after Deligne; arXiv v5 p. 4 and pp. 23–24
items.note: The degree of Z_k(p;T) is the Swan conductor of Sym^k Kl₂ at infinity, computed by Fu and Wan for odd p and by Yun for p = 2; the set S is exactly the set of primes at which the degree drops.

items.name: The Kloosterman connection and its symmetric powers
items.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, with π: G_m^{n+1} → G_m the first projection and f(z,x) = x₁ + ··· + x_n + z/(x₁···x_n), the Kloosterman connection is Kl_{n+1} = π_* E^f, a complex of D_{G_m}-modules. The cyclic cover [n+1]: t ↦ z = t^{n+1} gives Kl-tilde_{n+1} = [n+1]^* Kl_{n+1} = π-tilde_* E^{t g(y)} with g(y) = y₁ + ··· + y_n + 1/(y₁···y_n), and Kl_{n+1} is recovered as the μ_{n+1}-invariants of [n+1]_+ Kl-tilde_{n+1}.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §2.1; arXiv v5 p. 10
items.note: The change of variables x = ty is what turns f-tilde into the product t·g, which is the shape Theorem A.24 needs; this is the technical reason the whole argument passes to the cover.

items.name: Structure of the Kloosterman connection (Proposition 2.4)
items.statement: Kl_{n+1} is concentrated in degree zero and is the irreducible free O_{G_m}-module of rank n+1 with connection attached to the hypergeometric operator (z∂_z)^{n+1} - z; it has a regular singularity at z = 0 with unipotent monodromy and a single Jordan block, and an irregular singularity of pure slope 1/(n+1) at z = ∞; its dual is ι_{n+1}^* Kl_{n+1} for the involution z ↦ (-1)^{n+1}z; and Kl-tilde_{n+1} is the restriction to G_m of the Fourier transform of a regular holonomic D_{A¹}-module.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 2.4, with Lemma 2.5; arXiv v5 pp. 10–12
items.note: Proved by the recursion Kl_{n+2} ≅ ℱ inv^* Kl_{n+1} of Lemma 2.5, transposing Deligne's ℓ-adic arguments; clause (4) is what gives the symmetric powers their self-duality and clause (5) is what puts the whole computation inside the theory of mixed Hodge modules.

items.name: Irreducibility of the symmetric powers (Proposition 2.7)
items.statement: The connections Sym^k Kl_{n+1} and Sym^k Kl-tilde_{n+1} are irreducible.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 2.7; arXiv v5 p. 12
items.note: Irreducibility is what makes the intermediate extension at the origin equal to the minimal extension and is used repeatedly in §4.

items.name: Thom–Sebastiani for tensor powers (Proposition 2.10, Corollary 2.11)
items.statement: With f_k(z, x_{ji}) = Σ_j (Σ_i x_{ji} + z/∏_i x_{ji}) on G_m^{kn+1}, there are isomorphisms Kl_{n+1}^{⊗k} ≅ π_{k*}E^{f_k} and Kl-tilde_{n+1}^{⊗k} ≅ π-tilde_{k+}E^{f-tilde_k}, both concentrated in degree zero, and hence isomorphisms H¹_dR(G_m, Kl_{n+1}^{⊗k}) ≅ H^{kn+1}_dR(G_m^{kn+1}, E^{f_k}) and likewise for the tilde version.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 2.10 and Corollary 2.11; arXiv v5 pp. 13–14
items.note: This is the refined Künneth formula that turns the cohomology of a tensor power of connections into the twisted de Rham cohomology of a torus, which is what has an exponential-Hodge-theoretic meaning.

items.name: De Rham cohomology of the symmetric powers (Proposition 2.13)
items.statement: The de Rham cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} and of Sym^k Kl-tilde_{n+1} is concentrated in degree one, and H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) is the (𝔖_k, χ_n)-isotypic part of H^{kn+1}_dR(G_m^{kn+1}, E^{f_k}), equivalently the (𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n)-isotypic part of H^{kn+1}_dR(G_m^{kn+1}, E^{f-tilde_k}); the tilde version is the (𝔖_k, χ_n)-isotypic part of the latter.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 2.13; arXiv v5 pp. 15
items.note: Symmetric powers are read as isotypic parts of tensor powers, which is what makes the group actions on the hypersurface 𝒦 appear in Theorem 3.8.

items.name: Compactly supported and middle de Rham cohomology (Corollary 2.15)
items.statement: H^r_{dR,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) and H^r_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) vanish for r ≠ 1; the compactly supported group in degree one is the corresponding isotypic part of H^{kn+1}_{dR,c}(G_m^{kn+1}, E^{f_k}); the middle group equals H¹_dR(P¹, j_{!*}Sym^k Kl_{n+1}); and Poincaré duality induces a perfect (-1)^{kn+1}-symmetric pairing on it. The same holds for the tilde version.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 2.15; arXiv v5 pp. 15–16
items.note: The identification of the middle cohomology with the cohomology of the intermediate extension is what makes the terminology consistent with the ℓ-adic side, and the pairing is what gives the motive its essential self-duality.

items.name: The D-modules M and M-tilde and their Hodge module structure (Proposition 2.21, Lemma 2.24)
items.statement: Writing Kl-tilde_{n+1} as the restriction of a Fourier transform, one obtains D_{A¹}-modules M-tilde and Π(M-tilde) fitting in an exact sequence 0 → M-tilde → Π(M-tilde) → M-tilde' → 0 which underlies an exact sequence of mixed Hodge modules; M-tilde^H is the pure Hodge module W_{kn}Π(M-tilde^H) of weight kn and M-tilde'^H has weights ≥ kn+1, pure of weight 2k+1 when n = 1. Moreover M-tilde is irreducible and is the image of the canonical map from the ! to the * extension.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 2.21 and Lemma 2.24; arXiv v5 pp. 16–18
items.note: This is the object whose nearby cycles carry all the weight information; its purity is what Corollary A.31 is applied to.

items.name: The cohomologies of Sym^k Kl are classical mixed Hodge structures (Theorem 3.2)
items.statement: The exponential mixed Hodge structures H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}), H¹_c(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) and H¹_mid(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) are usual mixed Hodge structures, of weights ≥ kn+1, ≤ kn+1 and kn+1 respectively, the natural maps between them are morphisms of mixed Hodge structures, the induced map on gr^W_{kn+1} from the compactly supported to the ordinary one is an isomorphism, the middle one is its image, and it carries a (-1)^{kn+1}-symmetric pairing with values in Q(-kn-1). The same holds for Sym^k Kl-tilde_{n+1}.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 3.2; arXiv v5 pp. 19–21
items.note: The first of the paper's structural theorems. Its proof applies Theorem A.24 after the change of variables that makes the function of the form t·g, and then reduces purity to a dimension count comparing the Jordan blocks of the monodromy on nearby and vanishing cycles of M-tilde.

items.name: Geometric description of the middle Hodge structure (Theorem 3.8)
items.statement: Assume kn ≥ 2 and let 𝒦 ⊂ G_m^{kn} be the zero locus of the Laurent polynomial g^{⊞ k}(y) = Σ_{j=1}^k (Σ_{i=1}^n y_{ji} + ∏_{i=1}^n 1/y_{ji}), with the action of 𝔖_k × μ_{n+1} permuting the blocks and scaling by roots of unity. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of pure Hodge structures H¹_mid(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn-1}_c(𝒦)(-1)]^{𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n} ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}H^{kn+1}_{𝒦}(G_m^{kn})^{𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}, and if 𝒦 is smooth also to the same expression with ordinary cohomology.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 3.8; arXiv v5 pp. 21–23
items.note: This is what gives the Hodge structure a motivic origin and lets the paper define the middle motive 𝑴_k as the corresponding piece of the Nori motive of 𝒦. Remark 3.10 says 𝒦 has at worst isolated singularities, at the points whose coordinates are (n+1)-st roots of unity summing to zero; for n = 1 it is singular exactly when k is even.

items.name: The middle motive 𝑴_k
items.statement: 𝑴_k = gr^W_{kn+1}[𝑵^{kn-1}_c(𝒦)(-1)]^{𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}, the corresponding isotypic graded piece of the Nori motive of 𝒦 over Q, using the weight filtration on Nori motives.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), equation (3.1), §3 introduction, arXiv v5 p. 18
items.note: The object whose ℓ-adic realizations are the Galois representations r_{k,ℓ} of the introduction and whose Hodge realization is the middle Hodge structure.

items.name: The étale realization over a finite field (Theorem 3.12)
items.statement: Assume kn ≥ 2. There is a canonical isomorphism of Gal(F-bar_p/F_p)-modules between H¹_{ét,mid}(G_{m,F-bar_p}, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) and gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn-1}_{ét,c}(𝒦_{F-bar_p}, Q_ℓ(ζ))(-1)]^{𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}, and with the corresponding local-cohomology expression, and, when 𝒦 is smooth, with ordinary étale cohomology.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 3.12; arXiv v5 pp. 23–25
items.note: The ℓ-adic counterpart of Theorem 3.8, proved more easily because the formalism of weights is available regardless of ramification; it is what identifies the Frobenius traces of the motive with the moments.

items.name: Structure of the symmetric powers of Kl₂ (Proposition 4.6)
items.statement: Sym^k Kl₂ and Sym^k Kl-tilde₂ are free of rank k+1 with connection given in the bases u_a = v₀^{k−a}v₁^a and ũ_a = ṽ₀^{k−a}ṽ₁^a by z∂_z u_a = (k−a)u_{a+1} + a z u_{a−1} and ½t∂_t ũ_a = (k−a)ũ_{a+1} + a t² ũ_{a−1}; (1) their monodromy at the origin is unipotent with a single Jordan block of size k+1; (2) they carry (−1)^k-symmetric non-degenerate pairings induced by the skew self-duality of Kl₂; (3) formally at infinity Sym^k Kl̂₂ ≅ ⊕_{j=0}^{(k−1)/2}([2]_+E^{2(2j−k)t}) ⊗ L_i^{⊗k} for odd k and L_i^{⊗k} ⊕ ⊕_{j=0}^{k/2−1}([2]_+E^{2(2j−k)t}) ⊗ L_i^{⊗k} for even k (Lemma 4.7: Sym^k Kl̂₂ ≅ Sym^k([2]_+E^{2t}) ⊗ L_i^{⊗k} and [2]^+Sym^k([2]_+E^{2t}) ≅ ⊕_{j=0}^k E^{2(2j−k)t}); so irr_∞(Sym^k Kl₂) = ⌊(k+1)/2⌋, Sym^k Kl̂₂ is purely irregular for odd k, and for even k its regular part has rank one with formal monodromy of eigenvalue one iff 4 | k. Likewise irr_∞(Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) is k+1 for odd k and k for even k, and Sym^k Kl-tildê₂ ≅ ⊕_{j=0}^k E^{2(2j−k)t} ⊗ L_{−1}^{⊗k}.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 4.6, with Lemma 4.7; arXiv v5 pp. 27–28
items.note: The formal decomposition at infinity determines the dimension of the de Rham and middle cohomology and the behaviour of the intermediate extensions at infinity (Corollary 4.9). It uses the explicit structure of Kl₂ (item 71).

items.name: Intermediate extensions of the symmetric powers (Corollary 4.9)
items.statement: With j₀ and j_∞ the inclusions of G_m into the two affine charts, the map j_{∞!}Sym^k Kl₂ → j_{∞*}Sym^k Kl₂ is an isomorphism if k ≢ 0 mod 4, and for Sym^k Kl-tilde₂ if k is odd; and any proper submodule N of j_{0*}Sym^k Kl₂ with j₀^*N = Sym^k Kl₂ equals j_{0!}Sym^k Kl₂.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 4.9; arXiv v5 pp. 28–29
items.note: The first clause is the source of the exceptional behaviour when 4 | k, which is where the extra Hodge class of type (k/2+1, k/2+1) in Theorem 1.8 comes from.

items.name: The inverse Fourier transform of the symmetric powers (Corollary 4.10)
items.statement: For M-tilde the inverse Fourier transform of j_{0!*}Sym^k Kl-tilde₂ (the intermediate extension at the origin; §4 has n = 1): Π(M-tilde) is regular holonomic, generically of rank k+1, with singularities exactly at τ = 2(2j-k) for j = 0,…,k, vanishing cycle space of rank one at each with local monodromy (-1)^k, and unipotent monodromy at infinity with a single Jordan block of size k+1; M-tilde itself is generically of rank k with a single Jordan block of size k at infinity.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 4.10; arXiv v5 p. 29
items.note: The explicit local data that Corollary A.31 converts into Hodge numbers.

items.name: The dimension of the middle cohomology (Proposition 4.12)
items.statement: dim H¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) = ⌊(k-1)/2⌋ - δ_{4Z}(k), which is (k-1)/2 for odd k and 2⌊(k-1)/4⌋ for even k; and dim H¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) is k for odd k and k-2 for even k.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 4.12; arXiv v5 p. 30
items.note: This is the integer m of the introduction, the degree of M_k(p;T) for p outside S and the dimension of the Galois representations r_{k,ℓ}.

items.name: Bases of the de Rham cohomology (Proposition 4.14, Lemmas 4.15 and 4.17)
items.statement: H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) has basis the classes z^j u₀ dz/z = z^j v₀^k dz/z for 0 ≤ j < ⌊(k+1)/2⌋, and H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) the classes t^j ṽ₀^k dt/t for 0 ≤ j < 2⌊(k+1)/2⌋. Proof ingredients: H¹_dR is the cokernel of the injective z∂_z on G = Sym^k Kl₂; the inclusion of G⁺ = ⊕_i C[z]u_i (Deligne's canonical extension, residue nilpotent) is a quasi-isomorphism, since z∂_z acts invertibly on z^{−(r+1)}G⁺/z^{−r}G⁺ with eigenvalue −(r+1) (Lemma 4.15); for the grading deg z = 2, deg u_i = i, the graded map z∂_z-bar has determinant (k!!)²(−z)^{(k+1)/2} for odd k and zero for even k, and H⁰(gr G⁺, z∂_z-bar) = 0, H¹ = ⊕_{0≤j≤(k−1)/2} C z^j u₀ for odd k, while for even k both are free of rank one over C[z], generated by Σ_{i=0}^{k/2}(−1)^i C(k/2, i) z^i u_{k−2i} and by the class of u₀ (Lemma 4.17); the spectral sequence of the grading then gives the basis.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 4.14, Lemma 4.15 and Lemma 4.17; arXiv v5 pp. 30–32
items.note: These are the bases in which the Hodge filtration is written down in Proposition 4.21, which is the computational heart of the Hodge-number theorem.

items.name: Hodge numbers for the double cover (Proposition 4.20)
items.statement: H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) has weights ≥ k+1; for odd k it is mixed of weights k+1 and 2k+2 with one-dimensional (p,q)-parts for p+q = k+1 and p ∈ {1,…,k} and at (k+1,k+1); for even k it is mixed of weights k+1, k+2 and 2k+2, with the analogous parts omitting p = k/2, k/2+1 and with extra classes at (k/2+1, k/2+1) and (k+1, k+1). Moreover H¹_mid(G_m, Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) is pure of weight k+1 and equals W_{k+1} of the full group.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 4.20; arXiv v5 pp. 32–34
items.note: The computation on the cover, from which the statement downstairs follows by taking μ₂-invariants.

items.name: The Hodge filtration in the explicit bases (Proposition 4.21)
items.statement: In the bases of Proposition 4.14, F^p H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl-tilde₂) is spanned by the t^j e-tilde₀^k dt/t with 0 ≤ j ≤ k+1-p, and F^p H¹_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) by the z^j e₀^k dz/z with 0 ≤ j ≤ ⌊(k+1-p)/2⌋, for odd k, or for even k and p > k/2.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 4.21; arXiv v5 pp. 34–38
items.note: Proof of ⊇: the classes map to w_j = z^j dz/z·dx₁/x₁⋯dx_k/x_k and w-tilde_j = t^j dt/t·dy₁/y₁⋯dy_k/y_k in the twisted de Rham cohomology of the tensor powers, strictly for the irregular Hodge filtration; one needs w_j ∈ F^{k+1−2j} (j ≥ 0 for odd k, 2j ≤ k/2 for even k) and w-tilde_j ∈ F^{k+1−j} (j ≥ 0 for odd k, j ≤ k/2 for even k). For odd k this is the Newton filtration (item 64: h(z^j) = 2j for f_k, h-tilde(t^j) = j for f-tilde_k). For even k it comes from w-tilde_j ∈ Γ(X-tilde, Ω^{k+1}(log D)(jP − (k−j)E₁ − (k−2j)E₂)) on the compactification of item 72 and the log-pole description of item 73, then by pulling back along [2] for Sym^k Kl₂. Equality follows from the one-dimensionality of the graded pieces (Proposition 4.20).

items.name: Hodge numbers of the cohomology of the symmetric powers (Theorem 1.8)
items.statement: H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) has weights ≥ k+1. For odd k it is mixed of weights k+1 and 2k+2, with one-dimensional (p,q)-parts exactly for p+q = k+1 with p ∈ {2,4,…,k-1}, and at p = q = k+1. For even k it is mixed of weights k+1 and 2k+2 if k ≡ 2 mod 4, and of weights k+1, k+2 and 2k+2 if 4 | k, with one-dimensional parts exactly for p+q = k+1 with min{p,q} ∈ {2,4,…,2⌊(k-1)/4⌋}, at p = q = k/2+1 when 4 | k, and at p = q = k+1. Moreover H¹_mid(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) is pure of weight k+1 and equals W_{k+1}H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 1.8, proved in §4; arXiv v5 p. 7; proof pp. 37–38
items.note: The paper's central theorem. That every Hodge number is 0 or 1 is exactly the regularity of the Galois representations r_{k,ℓ}, which is what makes the Patrikis–Taylor theorem applicable.

items.name: Structure of the ℓ-adic realization for odd k (Theorem 5.8)
items.statement: Let k = 2m+1 be odd and p ≠ ℓ primes; V_{k,ℓ} is an m-dimensional Q_ℓ-representation of Gal(Q̄/Q) (item 76). (1) V_{k,ℓ} is unramified at 2 and V_{k,ℓ}[ζ] ≅ H¹_{ét,mid}(G_{m,F̄₂}, Sym^k Kl₂) as Gal(F̄₂/F₂)-modules. (2) For odd p, V_{k,ℓ} is at most tamely ramified at p, and its restriction to Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) is an orthogonal sum M ⊕ E with M[ζ] = H¹_{ét,mid}(G_{m,F̄_p}, Sym^k Kl₂) and E spanned by vanishing cycles, one for each odd a ≥ 1 with ap ≤ k, on which Galois acts by ε_a ⊗ χ_cyc^{−m−1}, ε_a the character of Q_p(√((−1)^{(1+ap)/2}2ap)). Writing E = E⁺ ⊕ E⁻ according as v_p(a) is odd (a ∈ Θ_p⁺) or even (a ∈ Θ_p⁻), V_{k,ℓ}^{I_p} = M ⊕ E⁺, and E⁺ is a semisimple Gal(F̄_p/F_p)-module with det(1 − F_pT | E⁺) = ∏_{a∈Θ_p⁺}(1 − ((−1)^{(1+ap)/2}2a'/p)p^{m+1}T), a' the prime-to-p part of a; |Θ_p⁺| + |Θ_p⁻| = ⌊k/2p + 1/2⌋.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 5.8, with Remarks 5.12 and 5.15; arXiv v5 pp. 42–44 (Remark 5.12, p. 44; Remark 5.15, p. 45)
items.note: Proof: for p = 2 the non-ordinary quadratic singularity of 𝒦̄_{F̄₂} (item 78) makes the specialization injective and a dimension count gives the isomorphism; for odd p, the Picard–Lefschetz sequence (item 77) with the ordinary quadratic points of item 75, orthogonality of the vanishing cycles to the image of H^{k−1}(𝒦̄_{F̄_p}), and the discriminant (−1)^{(k−ap)/2}2ap of the quadric 2apw² + Q_{ap} (T. Saito 2012, §5.2). Remark 5.12 gets the character by point counting and Chebotarev instead; Remark 5.15 notes the local factors and conductor are unchanged under semisimplification.

items.name: Structure of the ℓ-adic realization for even k (Theorem 5.17)
items.statement: Let k be even, k = 2m+2 or 2m+4 with m even, and p ≥ 3, ℓ distinct primes; V_{k,ℓ} is m-dimensional. Then I_p acts unipotently on V_{k,ℓ}: (σ − 1)² = 0 for σ ∈ I_p, and there is an isotropic subspace U ⊂ V_{k,ℓ} of dimension ⌊k/2p⌋, the image of the logarithm of the monodromy, spanned by vanishing cycles, with V_{k,ℓ}^{I_p} = U^⊥ and σ − 1: V_{k,ℓ} → V_{k,ℓ}/U zero. Moreover V_{k,ℓ}^{I_p}[ζ] ≅ H¹_{ét,c}(G_{m,F̄_p}, Sym^k Kl₂)/E[ζ] as Gal(F̄_p/F_p)-modules, where E = Q_ℓ(0) if 4 ∤ k and E is an extension of Q_ℓ(−k/2) by Q_ℓ(0) if 4 | k. In particular the Weil–Deligne representation of V_{k,ℓ} at p is pure of weight k+1.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 5.17; arXiv v5 pp. 45–48
items.note: Proof: pass to the resolution 𝒦' (item 79), use the Picard–Lefschetz formula σ(v) = v − (−1)^{k/2}t_ℓ(σ)Σ⟨v,δ_x⟩δ_x (item 77) and a weight and dimension count with (5.3); Frobenius acts on each vanishing cycle line by (−1)^{bp(p−1)/4}p^{(k−2)/2}, via the discriminant (−1)^{(k−bp)/2} of the quadric Q_{bp}. The prime 2 is left open, which is why Theorem 1.3 carries the unknown r_k and ε_k.

items.name: The p-adic realization is de Rham, and semistable or crystalline (Proposition 5.23)
items.statement: For every k and every prime p, the p-adic representation V_{k,p} of Gal(Q-bar_p/Q_p) is de Rham; for odd p it is semistable over Q_p(√-p) and there is an inclusion of Frobenius modules from H¹_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl₂) into the semistable module; and if p > k for odd k, respectively p > k/2 for even k, then V_{k,p} is crystalline and the two are isomorphic.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Proposition 5.23; arXiv v5 pp. 49–51
items.note: The bridge between the rigid cohomology of the Kloosterman F-isocrystal and the p-adic realization of the motive, which is what turns the Hodge numbers into a bound on Frobenius slopes.

items.name: Newton above Hodge for the moments (Corollary 5.27, Remark 5.28)
items.statement: For every k ≥ 1 and every odd prime p, the Newton polygon of the Frobenius module H¹_{rig,c}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl₂) lies above the Hodge polygon of H¹_{dR,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂), with coinciding endpoints when p > k for odd k or 2p > k for even k; consequently, writing Z_k(p;T) = Σ c_n T^n, one has v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n-1) for all p ≥ 3.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 5.27 and Remark 5.28; arXiv v5 p. 51
items.note: This sharpens a theorem of Haessig, who had the weaker bound (1 - 1/(p-1))n(n-1) for p ≥ 5 by Dwork-style p-adic analysis; the paper notes that Haessig proved the sharp bound for all p ≥ 2 while this paper was being refereed.

items.name: The gamma factor (Corollary 5.30)
items.statement: The gamma factor of 𝑴_k is L_k(∞,s) = π^{-ms/2}∏_{j=1}^m Γ((s-j)/2) with m = ⌊(k-1)/2⌋ - δ_{4Z}(k).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 5.30; arXiv v5 pp. 52–53
items.note: Computed from the Hodge numbers of Theorem 1.8 together with the action of complex conjugation on the Betti realization; this is the archimedean half of the completed L-function. The sign ε of σ on V^{w/2} (k = 4r+3) is −1: det σ = (−1)^rε, and det r_{k,ℓ} is the character of Q(√±k!!) by Fu–Wan's determinant formula (item 86). With Serre's Γ_V (item 87), Γ_V(s) = ∏_{j=1}^m Γ_R(s−j) = π^{m(m+1)/4}·π^{−ms/2}∏_{j=1}^mΓ((s−j)/2), so the printed formula omits the constant π^{m(m+1)/4} (recorded under sourceIssues; it does not affect the functional equation).

items.name: Potential automorphy for regular, pure, odd essentially self-dual systems (Theorem 5.38)
items.statement: Patrikis–Taylor (Th. A): let {r_ℓ: Gal(Q̄/Q) → GL_m(Q̄_ℓ)} be a weakly compatible system (for a finite S: r_ℓ unramified at p ∉ S for ℓ ≠ p with characteristic polynomial of Frobenius in Q[T] independent of ℓ; each r_ℓ de Rham, and crystalline for ℓ ∉ S; Hodge–Tate weights independent of ℓ) which is pure (the roots at p ∉ S are Weil numbers of one weight w), regular (m distinct Hodge–Tate weights) and odd essentially self-dual (all r_ℓ factor through GO_m(Q̄_ℓ) with even similitude character, or all through GSp_m(Q̄_ℓ) with odd similitude character, the characters forming a weakly compatible system). Then all r_ℓ become automorphic over a finite Galois totally real field, and L^S(𝓡, s) continues meromorphically to C.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Theorem 5.38, quoted from Patrikis–Taylor, Theorem A; arXiv v5 p. 56
items.note: The external input that converts the Hodge-number computation into the analytic continuation. Nothing in the atlas plans it: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 is the potential-automorphy assembly of the ten-author CM programme, a different theorem.

items.name: Meromorphic continuation and functional equation from potential automorphy (Corollary 5.39, Remark 5.41)
items.statement: For a weakly compatible system 𝓡 that is pure of weight w, regular and odd essentially self-dual, the Weil–Deligne representation WD_p(𝓡) at each p is pure of weight w, and the completed L-function Λ(𝓡, s) = L_∞(𝓡, s)∏_{p∈S}L(WD_p(𝓡), s)L^S(𝓡, s) satisfies Λ(𝓡, s) = ε(𝓡, s)Λ(𝓡^∨, 1 − s) (Patrikis–Taylor, Cor. 2.2(ii)). Potential automorphy also makes {r_{k,ℓ}} strictly compatible, so r_{k,p} is semistable over Q_p for even k and crystalline over Q_p(√−p) for odd k, and the Newton polygon of M_k(p;T) lies above the Hodge polygon of H¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) for all p (k odd) and all p ≠ 2 (k even) (Remark 5.41).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Corollary 5.39 and Remark 5.41, arXiv v5 pp. 57–59
items.note: Corollary 5.39 is what Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 are deduced from. The filtration lemma 5.40, which the checkpoint folded in here, is now its own item (89).

items.name: The Swan conductor of Sym^k Kl₂ at infinity and the degree of Z_k(p;T)
items.statement: deg Z_k(p;T) equals the Swan conductor of Sym^k Kl₂ at infinity, which for odd p is (k+1)/2 - ⌊k/2p + 1/2⌋ for odd k and k/2 - ⌊k/2p⌋ for even k, by Fu and Wan, and for p = 2 is (k+1)/2 for odd k and ⌊(k+2)/4⌋ for even k, by Yun; for p large compared with k it is ⌊(k+1)/2⌋.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.2, quoting Fu–Wan and Yun through the Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula; arXiv v5 pp. 4–5 and 39–40
items.note: The set S of bad primes is exactly the set where this degree drops below its generic value, so this computation is what defines the shape of the Euler product.

items.name: The Kloosterman F-isocrystal and its rigid cohomology
items.statement: Let ϖ ∈ Q̄_p with ϖ^{p−1} = −p (equivalently a non-trivial additive character of F_p) and K = Q_p(ϖ). Dwork's F-isocrystal AS_ϖ is the rank-one connection d + ϖdz on the overconvergent structure sheaf of A¹ over K with Frobenius structure exp(ϖ(z^p − z)), AS_{ϖh} = h^*AS_ϖ, and the Kloosterman F-isocrystal is Kl_{n+1} = Rπ_{rig*}AS_{ϖf}[n], of rank n+1 and pure of weight n (Crew). The rigid cohomology groups H¹_rig, H¹_{rig,c} and H¹_{rig,mid} of Sym^k Kl₂ carry Frobenius structures, and by Robba (Th. B) H¹_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl₂) = gr^W_{k+1}H¹_{rig,c}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl₂) has dimension ⌊(k−1)/2⌋ − δ_{4Z}(k) for p > k (k odd) and p > k/2 (k even).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.5
items.note: This is the p-adic avatar of the same object, needed because the ℓ-adic theory says nothing at ℓ = p; the comparison with the p-adic realization of the motive is Proposition 5.23.

items.name: ε-factors of the motive (§5.3.1, Remarks 5.35 and 5.37)
items.statement: With the Weil–Deligne representations and ε-factors of item 88 and ψ, dx fixed as there: (1) for odd k and 2 < p < ∞, N = 0, a(ρ) = |Θ_p⁻|, and ε_k(p,s) = w_p(p^{|Θ_p⁻|})^{(k+2)/2 − s} with w_p ∈ μ₄, w_p² = (−1, ±k!!)_p, the sign + if k ≡ 1, 7 mod 8; ε_k(p,s) = 1 where V_{k,ℓ} is unramified (including p = 2); ε_k(∞,s) = i^{(k²−1)/8}; hence ε_k(s) = ±cond_k^{(k+2)/2 − s}, unchanged under semisimplification. (2) For even k and 2 < p < ∞, a(ρ) = 0 and ε_k(p,s) = (−1)^{v_p}p^{⌊k/2p⌋((k+2)/2 − s)} with v_p = ⌊k/2p⌋ if p ≡ 1 mod 4 and ⌊k/4p⌋ if p ≡ 3 mod 4; ε_k(∞,s) = (−1)^{δ_{8Z}(k)}; so ∏_{2<p≤∞}ε_k(p,s) = (−1)^{v'}cond'_k^{(k+2)/2−s} with v' = Σ_{p≡1(4)}⌊k/2p⌋ + Σ_{p≡3(4)}⌊k/4p⌋ + δ_{8Z}(k). (3) If the functional equation L̂_k(s) = ε_k(s)L̂_k(k+2−s) holds with ε_k(s) = AB^{−s}, then A² = B^{k+2}; for even k at p = 2, with a = a(ρ), r = dim V^{ρ(I₂)}/ker(N)^{ρ(I₂)} and δ = det F₂ there, |δ| = 2^{r(k+2)/2} and ε_k(s) = w(2^{a+r}cond'_k)^{(k+2)/2−s}, w = (−1)^{v'}w'', |w''| = 1.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.1, arXiv v5 pp. 53–56, including Remarks 5.35 and 5.37
items.note: This is where the explicit conductors cond_k and cond'_k of the introduction come from, and where the unknown invariants r_k and ε_k at p = 2 for even k are isolated.

items.name: The Broadhurst–Roberts predictions for the remaining invariants
items.statement: Broadhurst and Roberts conjecture that for even k the invariants of Theorem 1.3 are r_k = ⌊k/6⌋ and ε_k = (-1)^{t_k} with t_k = ⌊k/8⌋ + Σ_{p ≡ 1 (4)} ⌊k/2p⌋ + Σ_{p ≡ 3 (4)} ⌊k/4p⌋ + δ_{8Z}(k); the paper shows that all terms of t_k other than ⌊k/8⌋ + δ_{8Z}(k) are accounted for by its computations at the odd primes of S and at infinity. Remark 5.37 adds that a + r = ⌊k/6⌋ (the exponent of 3 in cond'_k) and w'' = (−1)^{⌊k/8⌋} are conjectured, and that one structure fitting the data is V_{k,ℓ} tame at 2 with trivial inertia on the Weil–Deligne representation and det(1 − F₂T | V^{I₂}) = (1 − 2^{k/2}T)^{⌊k/8⌋}(1 + 2^{k/2}T)^{b_k}M_k(2;T), of degree (k−2)/2 − δ_{4Z}(k) − ⌊k/6⌋.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.1, arXiv v5 pp. 3–4, the paragraph after the even conductor, p. 49, and Remark 5.37, p. 56
items.note: Recorded as the remaining open part of the Broadhurst–Roberts conjecture, not as a theorem of the paper. The obstruction is the local computation at p = 2 for even k.

items.name: The toric interpretation of the irregular Hodge filtration
items.statement: For a Laurent polynomial φ on a torus G_m^N that is non-degenerate with respect to its Newton polytope Δ, with Newton degree h on the cone R_{≥0}Δ (the function equal to 1 on the facets of Δ not containing the origin), the irregular Hodge filtration on H^N_dR(G_m^N, E^φ) is induced by the Newton filtration on monomials of the cone R_{≥0}Δ (Adolphson–Sperber, Th. 1.4; Yu, Th. 4.6): a top form m·dz/z·dx₁/x₁⋯ with m in the cone and Newton degree h(m) whose class is non-zero lies in F^p for p ≤ N − h(m). For f_k = Σ_j(x_j + z/x_j) all monomials lie on h = 2α₀ + Σα_i = 1, the cone is cut out by the 2^k inequalities α₀ + Σε_iα_i ≥ 0 (ε_i ∈ {0,1}), and f_k is non-degenerate iff k is odd; for f-tilde_k one uses h-tilde = α₀, and f-tilde_k is non-degenerate for odd k.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.3, arXiv v5 p. 6, and §4.3.1, pp. 35–36, following Adolphson–Sperber and Yu
items.note: This is what makes the filtration computable, and is used together with the Hodge numbers of the cover to complete the proof of Theorem 1.8.

items.name: The sequel: Bessel moments and special values
items.statement: The determinants of Bessel moments ∫_0^∞ I_0(z)^a K_0(z)^{k-a} z^b dz/z conjecturally computed by Broadhurst and Roberts are related, through the periods of 𝑴_k, to the special values of L_k(s) at critical integers; this is the subject of the sequel paper.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.3, final paragraph; arXiv v5 p. 8
items.note: Recorded because the paper states it as the motivation for the Hodge-theoretic point of view; it is not proved here and belongs to the same lane as a later target.

items.name: Weil's bound for Kloosterman sums
items.statement: For a prime power q, a non-trivial additive character ψ of F_p and a ∈ F_q^×, Kl₂(a;q) = Σ_{x∈F_q^×}ψ(tr_{F_q/F_p}(x + a/x)) = −(α_a + β_a) with α_aβ_a = q and |α_a| = |β_a| = √q; in particular |Kl₂(a;q)| ≤ 2√q.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §1.1, arXiv v5 p. 2
items.note: FF.2 plans exponential-sum bounds for rational functions via curves and ℓ-adic trace functions; x + a/x is the basic case. The α_a, β_a are the Frobenius eigenvalues of the Kloosterman sheaf at a (item 33).

items.name: Katz: monodromy of Kloosterman connections and Kloosterman sheaves
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 the differential Galois group of Kl_{n+1}, and of Kl-tilde_{n+1}, is SL_{n+1}(C) if n is even and Sp_{n+1}(C) if n is odd (Katz 1987, Cor. 4.4.8, with Proposition 2.4(1)). For the ℓ-adic Kloosterman sheaf over F_p, the geometric monodromy group is SL_{n+1} or Sp_{n+1} over Q_ℓ(ζ) when p is odd or p = 2 and n is odd, and SO_{n+1} or G₂ when p = 2 and n is even (Katz 1988, Th. 11.1).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Proposition 2.7, arXiv v5 p. 12, and §3.2.1, p. 24
items.note: Since every symmetric power of the standard representation of SL_{n+1} or Sp_{n+1} is irreducible, this gives Proposition 2.7 and the concentration of the cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} in degree one; for p = 2 and n even the symmetric powers may contain the trivial representation, which is why §3.2.1 excludes that case.

items.name: Denef–Loeser: Gauss–Manin systems of a convenient non-degenerate Laurent polynomial
items.statement: Let h: G_m^N → A¹ be a Laurent polynomial that is convenient and non-degenerate with respect to its Newton polytope (for example g^{⊞k}). Then the cone of the natural morphism h_†O → h_+O has constant cohomology, so the kernel and cokernel of H⁰h_†O → H⁰h_+O are constant D_{A¹}-modules, and the image H⁰h_{†+}O becomes isomorphic to both after inverting ∂_τ. (Denef–Loeser, (3.6) and (3.9)(c), transposed to the complex setting: h extends to a proper h_Σ: Y_Σ → A¹ on a smooth toroidal variety with R^i(h_Σ restricted to each orbit closure)_*C constant, and h_Σ is proper and locally acyclic outside finitely many points.)
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Proposition 2.21 and its footnote, arXiv v5 pp. 16–17
items.note: Used to compare H⁰g^{⊞k}_{†+}O_U with FT^{−1}(j_{0+}Kl-tilde_{n+1}^{⊗k}) up to constant modules.

items.name: Katz's projector Π and the inverse Fourier transform
items.statement: On regular holonomic D_{A¹}-modules, Π(N) = N ⋆ j_{0†}O_{G_m} (additive *-convolution) is a projector onto the full subcategory of modules with vanishing global de Rham cohomology; the kernel and cokernel of N → Π(N) are constant; and Π∘FT^{−1} ≅ FT^{−1}∘j_{0+}j_0^+ (Katz 1990, Prop. 12.3.5). Hence, for M-tilde = FT^{−1}(j_{0†+}Sym^k Kl-tilde_{n+1}), Π(M-tilde) = FT^{−1}(j_{0+}Sym^k Kl-tilde_{n+1}) and 0 → M-tilde → Π(M-tilde) → M-tilde' → 0 with M-tilde' constant.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §2.3, arXiv v5 p. 16, and proof of Theorem A.24(2), p. 70
items.note: The D-module shadow of the projector Π_θ that defines EMHS (item 14).

items.name: Matsui–Takeuchi (appendix by Sabbah): weights of nearby cycles at infinity
items.statement: For n = 1, although Π(M-tilde^H) is only mixed, the weight filtration on ψ_{1/τ,1}Π(M-tilde^H) is the monodromy filtration of N centred at k, and ψ_{1/τ}M-tilde'^H is identified with the primitive part P_k gr^W_{2k}ψ_{1/τ,1}Π(M-tilde^H) (Matsui–Takeuchi, Prop. A.1 and the proof of Prop. A.3). As the monodromy at infinity has a single Jordan block (Corollary 4.10), M-tilde'^H is pure of weight 2k+1.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Proposition 2.21, arXiv v5 p. 18
items.note: The only input of Proposition 2.21 beyond Saito's theory; it concerns Gauss–Manin systems of Laurent polynomials in general.

items.name: Explicit structure of Kl₂ and Kl-tilde₂
items.statement: Kl₂ is the free C[z,z^{−1}]-module with basis v₀, v₁ (the classes of dx/x and x·dx/x in the cokernel of d + ∂_xf dx on C[x^{±1}, z^{±1}], f = x + z/x), with v₀ = e^{1/y}/y in j_0^+FT E^{1/y}, v₁ = z∂_z v₀ and z∂_z(v₀, v₁) = (v₀, v₁)(0 z; 1 0), so (z∂_z)²v₀ = zv₀; it lifts to a basis ṽ₀, ṽ₁ of Kl-tilde₂ with ½t∂_tṽ₀ = ṽ₁, ½t∂_tṽ₁ = t²ṽ₀. The isomorphism (v₀, v₁) ↦ (v₁^∨, −v₀^∨) gives a flat non-degenerate skew-symmetric pairing with ⟨v₀, v₁⟩ = 1. Formally at infinity Kl̂₂ ≅ [2]_+(E^{2t} ⊗ L_{−1}) ≅ ([2]_+E^{2t}) ⊗ L_i with L_{−1} = (C((t^{−1})), d + ½dt^{−1}/t^{−1}) and L_i = (C((z^{−1})), d + ¼dz^{−1}/z^{−1}), and Kl-tildê₂ ≅ (E^{2t} ⊕ E^{−2t}) ⊗ L_{−1}. For g = y + 1/y: G_m → A¹_τ, g_+O = O_{A¹} ⊕ M₂ with M₂ irreducible, of rank one on A¹ ∖ {±2} with monodromy −1 around ±2 and trivial monodromy at ∞; Kl-tilde₂ = j_0^+FT(M₂) and FT(M₂) = j_{0†+}Kl-tilde₂; the monodromy of ψ_zKl₂ and ψ_tKl-tilde₂ is unipotent with one Jordan block of size two.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §4.1, paragraphs on explicit bases, duality, the structure at infinity and Kl-tilde₂ as a localized Fourier transform, arXiv v5 pp. 26–27
items.note: The formal structure at infinity is the formal stationary phase formula (Sabbah 2008, Th. 5.1) applied to slope 1/2.

items.name: The toric compactification X of G_m^k and non-degenerate compactifications of (G_m^{k+1}, f-tilde_k)
items.statement: Following Mochizuki, a smooth compactification X of U, for f: U → A¹, is non-degenerate along D = X ∖ U if D is a strict normal crossing divisor and f extends to a rational map X ⇢ P¹ that, locally analytically, is 1/ξ^e or ζ₁/ξ^e in coordinates (ξ, η, ζ) with D = (ξη), e ∈ Z_{>0}^r. Let X be the toric variety of the simplicial fan in ⊕Re_i generated by the 3^k − 1 rays R_{≥0}Σε_ie_i (ε_i ∈ {0, ±1}, not all 0); it has 2^kk! maximal cones, each giving a chart ≅ A^k. On the chart of the cone spanned by e₁ + ⋯ + e_r (1 ≤ r ≤ k), with z_r = y_r/y_{r+1} (r < k) and z_k = y_k, g^{⊞k} = g₁/(z₁⋯z_k) where g₁ = 1 + Σ_{r=2}^k z₁⋯z_{r−1} + z₁⋯z_k Σ_{r=1}^k z_r⋯z_k; X is a non-degenerate compactification of (G_m^k, g^{⊞k}). Blowing up P¹_t × X successively along the intersections of the proper transform of 0 × X with those of P¹ × S_i, for the 3^k − 1 boundary components S_i, gives X̄, a non-degenerate compactification of (G_m^{k+1}, f-tilde_k) for odd k. For even k, X̄ is non-degenerate away from the C(k, k/2) points (t, y) = (∞, ε) with ε_i = ±1 and Σε_i = 0, which are ordinary quadratic points of g^{⊞k} = 0; blowing up these points and then the intersection of the exceptional divisor E₁ with the proper transform of ∞ × X (exceptional divisor E₂) gives a non-degenerate compactification X-tilde with ord_{E₁}f-tilde_k = 1 and ord_{E₂}f-tilde_k = 0.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §4.3.2, arXiv v5 pp. 35–36
items.note: Also used over Z in §5.1.2 to study the closure of 𝒦 (item 74).

items.name: The irregular Hodge filtration by log forms with poles on the pole divisor (Yu; Esnault–Sabbah–Yu)
items.statement: Let U be smooth quasi-projective, f: U → A¹, and X a non-degenerate compactification with D = X ∖ U and pole divisor P of f (defined since the indeterminacy locus of f: X ⇢ P¹ has codimension ≥ 2). Write Ω^i_X(log D)((i − p)P)₊ for Ω^i_X(log D)((i − p)P) if i ≥ p and 0 otherwise. If π: X' → X is a tower of blow-ups along intersections of the zero divisor with components of the pole divisor, with D' = X' ∖ U simple normal crossing and f extending to f': X' → P¹ with pole divisor P', then RΓ(X, (Ω^•_X(log D)((• − p)P)₊, d + df)) = RΓ(X', (Ω^•_{X'}(log D')((• − p)P')₊, d + df')) (Yu, Prop. 4.4, which does not need non-degeneracy of a Laurent polynomial), and by the E₁-degeneration of the irregular Hodge filtration (Esnault–Sabbah–Yu, Th. 1.2.2) the hypercohomology in degree r of the right-hand side is F^pH^r_dR(U, E^f). In particular every section of Ω^r_X(log D)((r − p)P) defines a class in F^pH^r_dR(U, E^f).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §4.3.3, arXiv v5 pp. 36–37
items.note: Applied with X = X-tilde, r = k+1 and p = k+1−j to the forms w-tilde_j (item 51).

items.name: The closure of 𝒦 in the toric compactification
items.statement: Let 𝒦 ⊂ G_m^k be the zero locus of g^{⊞k} = Σ_{i=1}^k(y_i + 1/y_i) and 𝒦̄ its closure in the toric compactification X of item 72, all over Z. Then 𝒦̄ is smooth along D = X ∖ G_m^k, each irreducible component of D meets 𝒦̄ in a smooth divisor, and 𝒦̄ ∖ 𝒦 is a relative strict normal crossing divisor over Z. Over Q, 𝒦 is smooth for odd k, and for even k its singular locus consists of the C(k, k/2) ordinary quadratic points with y_i ∈ {±1} and Σy_i = 0.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.1.2, arXiv v5 pp. 40–41; Remark 3.10, p. 22
items.note: Checked chart by chart on the 2^kk! charts; on X₁ one has (g₁) ∩ (z₁) = ∅, (g₁) ∩ (z_r) = (1 + z₁(1 + z₂ + ⋯ + z₂⋯z_{r−1})) and ∂g₁/∂z₁ restricted to (z_r) equal to 1 + z₂ + ⋯ + z₂⋯z_{r−1}, so ∂g₁/∂z₁ does not vanish on (g₁) ∩ (z_r). The printed sentence has two slips (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Singularities of 𝒦 over F̄_p
items.statement: Let p be odd. If k is odd, the singular locus Σ of 𝒦 over F̄_p consists of ⌊k/2p + 1/2⌋ orbits of ordinary quadratic points under 𝔖_k × μ₂, indexed by the odd a ≥ 1 with ap ≤ k and represented by y_i = 1 for i ≤ (ap+k)/2 and y_i = −1 otherwise; in the coordinates y_i = z_i ± 1 the equation of 𝒦 in Z_p[[z₁, …, z_k]] is 2ap + Q_{ap} + (higher order terms), Q_{ap} = Σ_{i≤(ap+k)/2}z_i² − Σ_{i>(ap+k)/2}z_i². If k is even, the singular locus of 𝒦_{F̄_p} consists of 1 + ⌊k/2p⌋ orbits of ordinary quadratic points indexed by the even b ≥ 0 with bp ≤ k, with local equation 2bp + Q_{bp} + (higher order terms). For p = 2 and odd k, 𝒦̄_{F̄₂} has a single isolated quadratic singularity, at y_i = 1, which is not ordinary.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.1.3, arXiv v5 p. 41; §5.1.4, p. 45; proof of Theorem 5.8, p. 43

items.name: The ℓ-adic realizations V_{k,ℓ} of 𝑴_k
items.statement: For a prime ℓ, V_{k,ℓ} = gr^W_{k−1}H^{k−1}_{ét,c}(𝒦_{Q̄}, Q_ℓ)^{𝔖_k×μ₂,χ}(−1), with the continuous representation r_{k,ℓ}: Gal(Q̄/Q) → GL(V_{k,ℓ}). Writing k = 2m+1 for odd k, and k = 2m+2 or 2m+4 with m even for even k, dim V_{k,ℓ} = m (Proposition 4.12).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), (5.5), §5.1.2, arXiv v5 p. 40

items.name: Picard–Lefschetz for ordinary quadratic points, with the Galois action through the discriminant
items.statement: Let Y be proper over a henselian trait with smooth generic fibre and special fibre of dimension N whose singular points Σ are ordinary quadratic, with local equations c + Q + (higher order terms). (1) If N = 2μ is even, there is an exact sequence 0 → H^N(Y_s̄) → H^N(Y_η̄) → ⊕_{x∈Σ}Q_ℓ(−μ) → 0 given by pairing with vanishing cycles δ_x ∈ H^N(Y_η̄)(μ), well defined up to sign, with ⟨δ_x, δ_y⟩ = (−1)^μ2 if x = y and 0 otherwise; Q_ℓ(−μ)δ_x is the primitive cohomology of the quadric D = (cw² + Q) of dimension N in P^{N+1}, and the Galois group of the fraction field acts on H^N_prim(D)(μ) = det H^N(D)(μ) through the quadratic character of the square root of (−1)^{(N+2)/2} times the discriminant of cw² + Q (T. Saito 2012, §5.2). (2) If N is odd, σ ∈ I acts by σ(v) = v − ε_N t_ℓ(σ)Σ_{x∈Σ}⟨v, δ_x⟩δ_x (the paper writes ε_N = (−1)^{(N+1)/2} for N = k − 1), and the line spanned by δ_x is the primitive cohomology H^{N−1}_prim(C) of the tangent quadric C = (Q) over the residue field, on which Frobenius acts by the Legendre symbol of (−1)^{(N+1)/2}·disc(Q) times p^{(N−1)/2}.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proofs of Theorems 5.8 and 5.17, arXiv v5 pp. 41–48, citing SGA 7 XV (Th. 3.4, Prop. 2.2.3) and T. Saito 2012
items.note: LPV.2 plans the ordinary quadratic singularity, the quadric cohomology, the five-term sequence, the odd-dimensional Picard–Lefschetz formula and the even-dimensional tame quadratic-character formula, with its sign table.

items.name: Vanishing cycles at an isolated quadratic singularity that is not ordinary (Illusie)
items.statement: Let Y be proper over a henselian trait, of relative dimension N, smooth except at one isolated singular point of the special fibre that is quadratic in Illusie's sense but not necessarily ordinary (as happens in residue characteristic 2, e.g. for 𝒦̄_{F̄₂} with k odd). Then the vanishing cycle sheaves R^nΦ vanish for n ≠ N (Illusie 2003, Cor. 2.10), so the specialization map H^N(Y_s̄) → H^N(Y_η̄) is injective.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Theorem 5.8(1), arXiv v5 p. 43
items.note: LPV.2 records the characteristic-2 distinction between a nonsingular quadric and a non-degenerate polar form but does not plan this non-ordinary case.

items.name: The resolution 𝒦' of 𝒦 for even k
items.statement: For even k ≥ 4, let S be the C(k, k/2) ordinary quadratic points of 𝒦 over Q, 𝒦' the strict transform of 𝒦 in the blow-up of G_m^k at S and T ⊂ 𝒦' the exceptional quadrics. As N^{k−2}(S) = N^{k−1}(S) = N^{k−1}(T) = 0, N_c^{k−1}(𝒦') ≅ N_c^{k−1}(𝒦) for Nori motives, and likewise for étale cohomology over Q̄ and F̄_p and for rigid cohomology. With 𝒦̄' the closure of 𝒦' in the blow-up of X along S and α: H_c^{k−1}(𝒦'_{Q̄}) → H^{k−1}(𝒦̄'_{Q̄}), V_{k,ℓ}(1) = im(α)^{𝔖_k×μ₂,χ}, and gr^W_{k−2}H_c^{k−1}(𝒦'_{Q̄})^{χ} has dimension δ_{4Z}(k).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Theorem 5.17, arXiv v5 pp. 45–46

items.name: Degrees and trivial factors of Z_k(p;T) (Fu–Wan, Yun)
items.statement: (1) For odd k, deg Z_k(p;T) = (k+1)/2 if p = 2 and (k+1)/2 − ⌊k/2p + 1/2⌋ if p ≥ 3, and Z_k(p;T) = (1 − T)M_k(p;T). (2) For even k and odd p, deg Z_k(p;T) = k/2 − ⌊k/2p⌋ and Z_k(p;T) = (1 − T)R_k(p;T)M_k(p;T) with R_k(p;T) = (1 − (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p^{k/2}T)^{n_k(p)}(1 − p^{k/2}T)^{m_k(p)−n_k(p)}, n_k(p) = ⌊k/4p + 1/2⌋, m_k(p) = ⌊k/2p⌋ + δ_{4Z}(k). (3) For even k and p = 2, deg Z_k(2;T) = ⌊(k+2)/4⌋ and Z_k(2;T) = (1 − T)(1 − 2^{k/2}T)^{a_k}(1 + 2^{k/2}T)^{b_k}M_k(2;T) with deg M_k(2;T) = 2⌊(k+2)/12⌋ − 2δ_{12Z}(k), a_k = ⌊k/24⌋ + 1 for k ≡ 0, 8, 12, 16, 18, 20 mod 24 and ⌊k/24⌋ otherwise, b_k = ⌊k/24⌋ + 1 for k ≡ 6, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22 mod 24 and ⌊k/24⌋ otherwise. In all cases the reciprocal roots of M_k(p;T) are Weil numbers of weight k+1, stable under α ↦ p^{k+1}α^{−1}.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.1.1, (5.1)–(5.4), arXiv v5 pp. 39–40
items.note: Quoted from Fu–Wan 2005, Th. 0.2, and Yun 2015, Lem. 4.2.1, Cor. 4.2.3, 4.3.4 and 4.3.5. The printed symmetry α ↦ p^{(k+1)/2}α^{−1} is a misprint (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Local L-factors and conductor for odd k
items.statement: For odd k = 2m+1: L_k(p;T)^{−1} = det(1 − F_pT | V_{k,ℓ}^{I_p}) equals M_k(2;T) for p = 2 and M_k(p;T)∏_{a∈Θ_p⁺}(1 − ((−1)^{(1+ap)/2}2a'/p)p^{m+1}T) for p ≥ 3; L_k(s) = ∏_pL_k(p;p^{−s}) converges absolutely for Re(s) > 1 + (k+1)/2. By Serre's recipe (Swan conductor plus codimension of the inertia invariants) the exponent of p in the conductor of {V_{k,ℓ}} is |Θ_p⁻| for odd p and 0 for p = 2, so cond_k = ∏_{p odd}p^{|Θ_p⁻|} = 1_s3_s5_s⋯k_s, where n_s is the product of the primes p with v_p(n) odd. Both are unchanged under semisimplification (Remark 5.15).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), (5.13), (5.14) and Remark 5.15, arXiv v5 pp. 44–45

items.name: Local L-factors and conductor for even k
items.statement: For even k and odd p: L_k(p;T)^{−1} = (1 − p^{k/2}T)^{⌊k/2p⌋}M_k(p;T) if p ≡ 1 mod 4 and (1 + p^{k/2}T)^{⌊k/4p+1/2⌋}(1 − p^{k/2}T)^{⌊k/2p⌋−⌊k/4p+1/2⌋}M_k(p;T) if p ≡ 3 mod 4; L_k(s) converges absolutely for Re(s) > 1 + (k+1)/2; the exponent of an odd p in the conductor is ⌊k/2p⌋, so the conductor is 2^{r_k}∏_{p odd}p^{⌊k/2p⌋} = 2^{r_k}·2_u4_u6_u⋯k_u, with n_u the product of the odd primes dividing n and r_k = Sw(V_{k,ℓ}|Gal(Q̄₂/Q₂)) + codim V_{k,ℓ}^{I₂}, which the paper does not determine.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), (5.22) and the conductor after it, arXiv v5 pp. 48–49

items.name: Rigid cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} through the hypersurface 𝒦
items.statement: With the Kloosterman F-isocrystal of item 61: for ? = ∅, c, mid, H¹_{rig,?}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) = H^{kn+1}_{rig,?}(G_m^{kn+1}/K, AS_{ϖf-tilde_k})^{𝔖_k×μ_{n+1},χ_n}; by Kedlaya's weights (the local contributions at 0 and ∞ have weights ≤ kn), H¹_{rig,mid} ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}H^{kn+1}_{rig,c}(G_m^{kn+1}/K, AS_{ϖf-tilde_k})^{χ_n}; and by the localization sequences of rigid cohomology (Le Stum, Prop. 8.2.18(ii)) and the Gysin isomorphism (Tsuzuki, Th. 4.1.1), H¹_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn−1}_{rig,c}(𝒦/K)(−1)]^{𝔖_k×μ_{n+1},χ_n} ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}H^{kn+1}_{rig,𝒦}(G_m^{kn}/K)^{𝔖_k×μ_{n+1},χ_n}, and ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn−1}_rig(𝒦/K)(−1)]^{χ_n} when 𝒦 is smooth.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §3.2.2, (3.13)–(3.14), arXiv v5 pp. 25–26

items.name: Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula and semistable reduction
items.statement: Let p be odd and L = Q_p(√−p) = Q_p(ϖ^{(p−1)/2}). Over Z_p[√−p], each ordinary quadratic point of 𝒦̄' (𝒦̄ for odd k) is formally defined by Q − u(√−p)² with u a unit and Q = Q_{ap} or Q_{bp} defining a smooth quadric in P^{k−1}; the blow-up 𝒦̄'' of 𝒦̄' ⊗ Z_p[√−p] at these points is semistable, and there is a commutative diagram of L-modules in which the map β: H^{k−1}_rig(𝒦̄'_{F_p}/Q_p)_L → H^{k−1}_dR(𝒦̄'_{Q_p})_L is injective and compatible with Frobenius (constructed with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes) and restricts on the kernels of the differentials to the boundary strata (Mieda 2007, Th. 1.1 and (2.3)). For even k and p > k/2 (odd k and p > k), 𝒦̄' is smooth and β is induced by the rigid–de Rham isomorphism.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Proposition 5.23, arXiv v5 pp. 49–51

items.name: p-adic comparison theorems for the varieties 𝒦̄, 𝒦̄' and 𝒦̄''
