items.statement: The p-adic étale cohomology of a smooth proper variety over Q_p is de Rham with D_dR = de Rham cohomology; for a proper semistable model over the ring of integers of a finite extension L of Q_p, every subquotient of the p-adic étale cohomology of the generic fibre is a semistable Gal(Q̄_p/L)-representation, with D_st given by the log-crystalline (Hyodo–Kato) cohomology of the special fibre, compatibly with Frobenius; with good reduction it is crystalline with D_crys the crystalline (= rigid) cohomology of the special fibre (as cited from Beilinson 2013, §3.3(i), (iii) and §3.4).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Proposition 5.23 and §5.3.3, arXiv v5 pp. 49–51 and 57
items.note: CP.3 plans the de Rham comparison, CP.4 the semistable (B_st) comparison with Frobenius and monodromy, and CP.2 the crystalline case (CP.4 names good reduction as recovering CP.2).

items.name: Fu–Wan's determinant and the determinant of r_{k,ℓ}
items.statement: For odd k and odd p, det(F_p | H¹_{ét,mid}(G_{m,F̄_p}, Sym^k Kl₂)) = p^{(k+1)dim H¹_mid/2}(2/p)^{⌊k/2p+1/2⌋}∏_{0≤j≤(k−1)/2, p∤2j+1}((−1)^j(2j+1)/p) (Fu–Wan 2010, Th. 0.1). Hence for p > k, det r_{k,ℓ}(Frob_p) = (p/k!!)p^{(k²−1)/4} with k!! = 3·5⋯k, and by Chebotarev det r_{k,ℓ} = (·/k!!)χ_cyc^{(1−k²)/4}, the character of Q(√±k!!) with the sign making the radicand ≡ 1 mod 4 (namely + iff k ≡ 1, 7 mod 8).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), proof of Corollary 5.30, arXiv v5 pp. 52–53, and §5.3.1, p. 55

items.name: Serre's gamma factor of an R-Hodge decomposition
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space V with a grading V = ⊕_pV^p and a C-linear involution σ with σ(V^p) = V^{w−p} (an R-Hodge decomposition of weight w), set h(p) = dim V^p, h(w/2)^± = dim{v ∈ V^{w/2} : σv = ±(−1)^{w/2}v} for even w (and 0 for odd w), Γ_R(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2), Γ_C(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s) = Γ_R(s)Γ_R(s+1), and Γ_V(s) = Γ_R(s − w/2)^{h(w/2)⁺}Γ_R(s − w/2 + 1)^{h(w/2)⁻}∏_{p<w/2}Γ_C(s − p)^{h(p)}. For 𝑴_k, V^p = gr^p_FH¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂), w = k+1, and σ is induced by complex conjugation on H^{k−1}(𝒦(C)) and H^{k−1}_c(𝒦(C)).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.2, arXiv v5 p. 52, after Serre 1970, §3

items.name: Weil–Deligne representations and Deligne's local ε-factors
items.statement: For p < ∞, ψ is Q_p → Q_p/Z_p = Z[1/p]/Z → C^×, α ↦ exp(2πiα), and dx the self-dual Haar measure with ∫_{Z_p}dx = 1; at ∞, ψ(α) = exp(−2πiα) and dx is Lebesgue measure. W(Q̄_p/Q_p) is the Weil group, with local class field theory normalized so that p ↦ geometric Frobenius F_p, and ω_s(α) = ‖α‖^s. A Weil representation ρ has ε₀(ρ, s) = ε₀(ρω_s, 0) (Deligne 1973, Th. 4.1) and ε₀(ρ, s) = p^{−a(ρ)s}ε₀(ρ, 0), a(ρ) the conductor. A Weil–Deligne representation (ρ, N) satisfies ρ(w)Nρ(w)^{−1} = p^{−v(w)}N; from an ℓ-adic representation r (ℓ ≠ p), Grothendieck's quasi-unipotence gives N with r(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) on an open subgroup of I_p and ρ(σF_p^n) = r(σF_p^n)exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N). Then ε₁((ρ, N), s) = det(−p^{−s}F_p | V^{ρ(I_p)}/ker(N)^{ρ(I_p)}), ε((ρ, N), s) = ε₀(ρ, s)ε₁((ρ, N), s) (Deligne 1979, before Rem. 5.2.1), and V^{r(I_p)} = ker(N)^{ρ(I_p)}. (ρ, N) is pure of weight w if F_p has Weil numbers of weight w + a on the graded pieces V^{≤a}/V^{≤a−1} of the monodromy filtration of N.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.1, arXiv v5 pp. 53–54, and §5.3.2, p. 57
items.note: R01.2 plans quasi-unipotence and the Weil–Deligne representation of an ℓ-adic representation; ET.6 plans local constants on the Weil–Deligne side.

items.name: Lemma 5.40: a representation whose graded Weil–Deligne representation is pure
items.statement: Let p ≠ ℓ be primes and r: Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) → GL(V) an ℓ-adic representation with a filtration 0 = V₀ ⊂ V₁ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_c = V by stable subspaces such that the Weil–Deligne representation of the induced r̄ on V̄ = ⊕_iV_i/V_{i−1} is pure. Then the Weil–Deligne representation of r is pure, and r and r̄ have the same L- and ε-factors.
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), Lemma 5.40, arXiv v5 p. 58
items.note: Proved in the paper (from a referee's sketch): ε₀ depends only on the semisimplification, N restricts to the logarithm of monodromy on each V_i, the relation Nφ = pφN spreads eigenvalues along the monodromy filtration, and taking I_p-invariants is exact on Weil representations. Used for even k to replace {r_{k,ℓ}} by its semisimplification.

items.name: The system {r^ss_{k,ℓ}} satisfies the hypotheses of the Patrikis–Taylor theorem
items.statement: For each k ≥ 1 the r_{k,ℓ} are pure of weight k+1. The p-adic comparison gives a filtered isomorphism (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_dR)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} ⊗ C ≅ gr^W_{k−1}H^{k−1}_{dR,c}(𝒦_{Q_p})^{𝔖_k×μ₂,χ}(−1) ⊗ C ≅ H¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂), so the Hodge–Tate weights of V_{k,p} are the a with gr^a_F ≠ 0, each of multiplicity one by Theorem 1.8 (regularity). The (−1)^{k+1}-symmetric pairing (3.4) makes r_{k,ℓ} factor through GO_m(Q̄_ℓ) (k odd) or GSp_m(Q̄_ℓ) (k even) with similitude χ_cyc^{−k−1}, and so does r^ss_{k,ℓ} (Serre 2018, Th. 4.2.1). The r^ss_{k,ℓ} are de Rham, crystalline for ℓ > k (Proposition 5.23), and form a weakly compatible system; their L- and ε-factors equal those of r_{k,ℓ} (Remarks 5.15 and 5.35 for odd k, Lemma 5.40 for even k).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.3, arXiv v5 pp. 57–58

items.name: Semisimplification preserves orthogonal and symplectic similitude structures (Serre)
items.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional representation over a field of characteristic zero of a group G with a character χ, carrying a non-degenerate symmetric (resp. alternating) bilinear form with ⟨gv, gw⟩ = χ(g)⟨v, w⟩. Then the semisimplification of V carries a non-degenerate symmetric (resp. alternating) form with the same similitude character (Serre 2018, Th. 4.2.1, applied to the group ring with the involution g ↦ χ(g)g^{−1}).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.3, arXiv v5 p. 57

items.name: T. Saito: the sign of the functional equation of an orthogonal motive
items.statement: The sign of the functional equation of the L-function of an orthogonal motive of even weight over Q (a motive with a non-degenerate symmetric pairing to Q(−w), w even), whenever that functional equation holds, is +1 (T. Saito 1995).
items.locator: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, published version (arXiv:1810.06454v5), §5.3.3, arXiv v5 p. 58
items.note: This is what fixes the sign in Theorem 1.2 for odd k, where 𝑴_k has even weight k+1 and a symmetric pairing.

routes.title: Mixed Hodge modules, exponential mixed Hodge structures and the irregular Hodge filtration
routes.brief: Plan the theory of mixed Hodge modules on a curve, exponential mixed Hodge structures and the irregular Hodge filtration, to the depth at which they can be used. The atlas has nothing on D-modules: a search of data/atlas.json for "D-module", "hodge module", "irregular hodge" and "exponential motive" returns nothing relevant, and the only hits for "vanishing cycle" are the ℓ-adic ones of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles and WeightsInEtaleCohomology. Construct, in order. Algebraic D-modules on a smooth variety over a field of characteristic zero: holonomic and regular holonomic modules, the derived direct and inverse images for an open immersion, the functors j_!, j_* and the intermediate extension j_{!*}, duality, and, at an irregular singular point of a meromorphic connection on a curve, the slope decomposition and the formal decomposition of Levelt and Turrittin. Then the Fourier transformation FT of holonomic D-modules on the affine line, exchanging t and ∂_t with τ and -∂_τ, its localized form ℱ = j_0^* FT j_{0*} on G_m, the fact that ℱ preserves holonomicity and sends a regular holonomic module to one smooth on G_m with a regular singularity at the origin and slopes in {0,1} at infinity, and the compatibility of FT with duality up to t ↦ -t. Then Saito's category MHM(X) of mixed Hodge modules: the underlying filtered D-module and rational perverse sheaf, the weight filtration, pure Hodge modules, the six operations, and the nearby- and vanishing-cycle functors ψ and φ with their monodromy weight filtrations and the Lefschetz decomposition of the associated graded. The final statements are those of the appendix of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, which is where the theory is assembled for use. Define the category EMHS of exponential mixed Hodge structures of Kontsevich and Soibelman as the image of the projector Π on MHM(A¹), with its tensor structure and its own weight filtration; prove the comparison of that filtration with the one of MHM(A¹) (Remark A.6), in particular that Π of a pure Hodge module of weight n is pure of weight n in EMHS although only mixed of weights ≥ n in MHM(A¹). Define the irregular Hodge filtration on H¹_dR(A¹_t, N ⊗ E^t) after Deligne, Sabbah and Yu, and prove that the bifiltered de Rham fibre factors through Π and that every morphism is strictly bifiltered (Proposition A.10). Prove that mixed Hodge structures form a full tensor subcategory of EMHS compatibly with weights (Lemma A.12) and that, for an object of EMHS that is classical, the irregular Hodge filtration is the ordinary Hodge filtration of φ_{t,1} (Proposition A.13). Define, for a smooth quasi-projective U with a regular function f, the objects H^r(U,f), H^r_c(U,f) and H^r_mid(U,f) of EMHS with their twisted de Rham fibres (Definition A.18), and prove the weight statement and the purity criterion of Proposition A.19, the localization sequences of Example A.20, and the basic computation H^k(G_m^k, x₁+···+x_k) ≅ Q(-k) of Example A.22. Prove the criterion that an exponential mixed Hodge structure attached to a function of the form t·g is classical (Theorem A.24) and the identification of its compactly supported cohomology with that of the zero locus of g (Example A.27). Finally prove the Hodge-theoretic form of the Fourier transform (Lemma A.28, Notation A.29, Theorem A.30) and the weight computation for the Fourier transform of a pure Hodge module in terms of the monodromy filtration on nearby cycles (Corollary A.31). Add the two computational descriptions of the irregular Hodge filtration: by the Newton filtration for Laurent polynomials that are non-degenerate with respect to their Newton polytope (Adolphson–Sperber, Yu), and by logarithmic forms with poles along the pole divisor on a non-degenerate compactification, independent of the chosen resolution of indeterminacy (Yu, Prop. 4.4), with the E₁-degeneration of Esnault–Sabbah–Yu. Add the three D-module inputs of the paper's §2.3: Katz's projector Π with Π∘FT^{−1} ≅ FT^{−1}∘j_{0+}j_0^+ (Katz 1990, Prop. 12.3.5); Denef–Loeser's theorem that the Gauss–Manin systems h_† and h_+ of a convenient non-degenerate Laurent polynomial differ by constant modules; and the Matsui–Takeuchi–Sabbah identification of the weight filtration on nearby cycles at infinity of Π of such a Gauss–Manin system with a shifted monodromy filtration. Scope of Saito's theory, which nothing in the atlas plans and which this roadmap must therefore build rather than import: the paper uses mixed Hodge modules on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with the underlying filtered D-module and Q-perverse sheaf; pure polarizable Hodge modules and their semisimplicity (decomposition by strict support); the weight filtration; the functors f_*, f_!, f^*, f^!, 𝐃 and ⊠ on D^b(MHM) with the weight bounds for f_! and f_* (Saito 1990, (4.5.2)); the localization triangles (Saito 1990, (4.4.1)); ψ_f, φ_{f,1}, can, var and the relative monodromy weight filtration; on curves, the compatibility rk gr^p_F M = dim gr^p_F ψ_f M (Saito 1988, 3.2.1); and the lift of additive convolution and Π to MHM(A¹). The decomposition theorem and mixed Hodge modules on singular varieties are not used and are not in scope. Import, and do not rebuild: pure and mixed Hodge structures with their weight filtrations and Deligne's strictness from Tau Ceti, where they exist at the pinned commit (TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure and its strictness theorems); nearby and vanishing cycles in the topological and ℓ-adic settings from LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 and LPV.6 and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.3; the perverse category and the intermediate extension from EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5, and Poincaré duality from EDC.2. Do not plan the Kloosterman computation here: it is the separate roadmap KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy proposed by this extraction, which is this lane's first consumer.

Searching data/atlas.json, "hodge module" and "exponential motive" return nothing; "d-module" returns seven hits, none of them about D-modules in this sense; "irregular" returns the irregularity of a Fuchsian equation in modular-forms layers and the irregular-radius theory of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.1, which is the p-adic analogue, not this one. Among the pending proposals, HodgeStructuresPartII from PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24 plans variations of Hodge structure, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory, which is a different extension of the Tau Ceti Hodge-structures roadmap and does not contain Saito's mixed Hodge modules; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCyclesPartIIGeneralBasesFourier and the perverse-sheaf Part IIs are ℓ-adic. This is a new roadmap rather than a Part II of the Tau Ceti Hodge-structures roadmap because its subject is not Hodge structures but the sheaf-theoretic theory over them, together with the D-module theory that theory is built on, and because it has an endpoint of its own: the appendix's criterion for an exponential mixed Hodge structure to be classical, with the irregular Hodge filtration agreeing with the Hodge filtration. It is separated from the Kloosterman computation because it is general machinery that many other papers in the queue on exponential motives and irregular Hodge theory will need.

routes.title: Symmetric power moments of Kloosterman sums: Hodge numbers, motives and potential automorphy
routes.brief: Plan the Hodge theory of Kloosterman connections and the resulting L-functions of symmetric power moments of Kloosterman sums. Fix a prime p, a non-trivial additive character ψ of F_p and, for a ∈ F_q^×, the Kloosterman sum Kl₂(a;q) = Σ_{x} ψ(tr(x + a/x)); write Kl₂(a;q) = -(α_a + β_a) with α_aβ_a = q, form the symmetric powers and the moments m₂^k(q), and let Z_k(p;T) be their generating polynomial and M_k(p;T) the factor left after removing the trivial factors. The final theorems are the three results of Fresán, Sabbah and Yu. (1) Theorem 1.8, the Hodge-number theorem: the mixed Hodge structure H¹(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂) has weights ≥ k+1 and all its Hodge numbers are 0 or 1, with the explicit list given there, and H¹_mid is pure of weight k+1 and equals W_{k+1} of it. (2) Theorem 1.2: for odd k the L-function L_k(s) continues meromorphically and Λ_k(s) = Λ_k(k+2-s). (3) Theorem 1.3: for even k it continues meromorphically and satisfies Λ_k(s) = ε_kΛ_k(k+2-s) for a sign ε_k and an unknown local factor at 2. These are the functional equations conjectured numerically by Broadhurst and Roberts; the remaining part of their conjecture, the values r_k = ⌊k/6⌋ and ε_k = (-1)^{t_k}, should be recorded as an open boundary, not a target. Cover, in order. The Kloosterman sheaf of Deligne and the cohomological interpretation Z_k(p;T) = det(1 - F_pT | H¹_{ét,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂)), with M_k(p;T) the same determinant on the middle cohomology and its purity of weight k+1; the Swan conductor computations of Fu–Wan and Yun that give the degree and define the bad set S. The Kloosterman connection Kl_{n+1} = π_*E^f on G_m over a field of characteristic zero, its pullback Kl-tilde_{n+1} along the cyclic cover z = t^{n+1}, and the change of variables that turns the function into t·g; the structure theorem, that Kl_{n+1} is the irreducible rank-(n+1) connection of the hypergeometric operator (z∂_z)^{n+1} - z, regular with a single unipotent Jordan block at 0, of pure slope 1/(n+1) at infinity, self-dual up to an involution, and the restriction of a Fourier transform of a regular holonomic module; and the irreducibility of the symmetric powers. The Thom–Sebastiani description of the tensor powers and the resulting identification of the de Rham cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} with an isotypic part of the twisted de Rham cohomology of a torus, the vanishing outside degree one, and the Poincaré pairing on the middle part. Then the Hodge theory: that all three cohomologies are classical mixed Hodge structures with the stated weights and that the middle one is pure (Theorem 3.2); the geometric description of the middle Hodge structure by the hypersurface 𝒦 ⊂ G_m^{kn} cut out by g^{⊞ k} with its 𝔖_k × μ_{n+1}-action (Theorem 3.8), the location of its singular points, the definition of the middle motive 𝑴_k as the corresponding piece of the Nori motive of 𝒦, and the étale counterpart over a finite field (Theorem 3.12). Then the explicit computation for n = 1: the formal structure of Sym^k Kl₂ at infinity, the behaviour of the intermediate extensions and the exceptional case 4 | k, the inverse Fourier transform with its singularities at τ = 2(2j-k), the dimension formula ⌊(k-1)/2⌋ - δ_{4Z}(k), the explicit bases of the de Rham cohomology and the Hodge filtration in them, and the Hodge numbers on the double cover, from which Theorem 1.8 follows by taking invariants. The n = 1 computation also needs the explicit bases, duality and formal structure of Kl₂ and Kl-tilde₂ and the Fourier description Kl-tilde₂ = j_0^+FT(M₂) for g = y + 1/y; the toric compactification X of G_m^k (the fan with the 3^k − 1 rays Σε_ie_i) and the non-degenerate compactifications X̄ and X-tilde of (G_m^{k+1}, f-tilde_k) in Mochizuki's sense; and Katz's monodromy groups of Kloosterman connections and sheaves. Finally the arithmetic: the closure 𝒦̄ of 𝒦 in X over Z (smooth along the boundary, a relative strict normal crossing divisor), the ordinary quadratic singularities of 𝒦 over F̄_p (⌊k/2p + 1/2⌋ orbits for odd k, 1 + ⌊k/2p⌋ for even k, with local equations 2ap + Q_{ap} and 2bp + Q_{bp}) and the non-ordinary one over F̄₂, the resolution 𝒦' for even k, the realizations V_{k,ℓ} (5.5), the factorization of Z_k(p;T) of Fu–Wan and Yun, the local L-factors and conductors cond_k = 1_s3_s⋯k_s and 2^{r_k}·2_u4_u⋯k_u, Fu–Wan's determinant formula and det r_{k,ℓ}, Serre's gamma factor, the ε-factors, Serre's theorem that semisimplification preserves orthogonal and symplectic similitude structures, T. Saito's theorem on the sign for orthogonal motives, and the verification that {r^ss_{k,ℓ}} satisfies the Patrikis–Taylor hypotheses. Then: the ℓ-adic realizations V_{k,ℓ} of 𝑴_k with their ramification at the bad primes, tame for odd k and unipotent for even k; the p-adic realization, its de Rham, semistable and crystalline properties and the comparison with rigid cohomology; the gamma factor read off the Hodge numbers; the local L- and ε-factors; and the deduction of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 from the potential automorphy of the compatible system {r_{k,ℓ}}. routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas follows this proof. "kloosterman" returns one unrelated hit in a partition-asymptotics layer. No layer and no pending proposal plans the Kloosterman sheaf or connection, its symmetric powers, their cohomology, or the motives of symmetric power moments. The L-function side is equally uncovered: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 and ML.3 own the potential-automorphy assembly of the CM programme and symmetric powers of modular forms, not a compatible system attached to a rigid motive of this kind. It is a new roadmap rather than a Part II because its two endpoints, the Hodge-number theorem and the Broadhurst–Roberts functional equations, belong to no existing direction, and because it is the first consumer of the general machinery this extraction proposes alongside it. The two are kept apart so that the machinery is reusable and the application stays honest about what it imports.

ML.2 is the potential-automorphy assembly of the campaign. The two items routed here are Patrikis and Taylor's theorem, that a weakly compatible system which is pure, regular and odd essentially self-dual becomes automorphic over a finite totally real Galois extension, and its corollary on the purity of the Weil–Deligne representations, the functional equation of the completed L-function and strict compatibility. §5.3.2 of the paper quotes both with their exact hypotheses and §5.3.3 applies them, so it is a good source for that layer; nothing else in the atlas plans them.

RD.6 plans the trace formula, the Fourier transform and Kedlaya's p-adic weights, and RD.7 the crystalline comparison and the export of Weil factors. The items routed here are the Kloosterman F-isocrystal with Robba's dimension count for the middle rigid cohomology of its symmetric powers, the expression of that cohomology through the hypersurface 𝒦 (by weights, localization and the Gysin isomorphism), Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula with the semistable model obtained by blowing up the ordinary quadratic points over Z_p[√−p], the comparison of rigid cohomology with the p-adic realization through B_st and B_crys, and the resulting Newton-above-Hodge inequality v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n−1). §§3.2.2 and 5.1.5 of the paper are a clean source for all of them.

LPV.2 plans ordinary quadratic singularities, the cohomology of the tangent quadric, the five-term specialization sequence, the odd-dimensional Picard–Lefschetz formula and the even-dimensional tame quadratic-character formula, and it notes the characteristic-2 distinction between nonsingular quadrics and non-degenerate polar forms. The paper uses exactly these, with the discriminant computation of T. Saito, and in characteristic 2 it also needs Illusie's theorem that the vanishing cycles at an isolated quadratic singularity that is not ordinary are concentrated in the middle degree, which LPV.2 does not plan. The missing item is that theorem; the planned item is listed because §5.1 is a worked source for LPV.2.

R01.2 plans decomposition and inertia groups, quasi-unipotence, the Weil–Deligne representation of an ℓ-adic representation, and the distinction between a representation, its semisimplification and its Frobenius semisimplification. Lemma 5.40, that an ℓ-adic representation with a filtration whose graded Weil–Deligne representation is pure is itself pure with the same L- and ε-factors, is a general statement of exactly this kind, which the paper proves in full; the planned item is the Weil–Deligne and ε-factor formalism of §5.3.1.
